A propositional formula is a logical statement that is either true or false. It is built from propositional variables, logical connectives, and logical quantifiers, and it asserts something about whether a proposition holds. Propositional variables are symbols standing for a proposition or claim; "p" and "q," for instance, are propositional variables. Logical connectives are symbols that join two or more propositions in a logically meaningful way. Several kinds exist, namely conjunction (and), disjunction (or), negation (not), implication (if-then), and equivalence (if and only if). Logical quantifiers are symbols that indicate the scope of a propositional variable, and there are two kinds: the universal quantifier (for all) and the existential quantifier (there exists). As an illustration, consider the formula "If p, then q." It is made up of the propositional variables "p" and "q," the if-then connective, and the words "if" and "then" acting as quantifiers. Across logic and computer science, propositional formulas serve to represent and reason about whether propositions are true or false. They provide a precise, formal way to express logical statements, and by applying the rules of logic to them, one can derive conclusions about the truth or falsity of propositions.

Your message is just the phrase "reporting software subscriptions," so I'll assume you want a useful overview of the topic and you can steer me toward something more specific afterward.

Reporting software is typically sold on a subscription basis in a few common pricing models. Per-user pricing charges for each person who creates or views reports, often with cheaper tiers for view-only users. Tiered plans bundle features such as data connectors, refresh frequency, row limits, and white-labeling into packages like starter, professional, and enterprise. Usage-based pricing charges by data volume, number of queries, or number of reports generated, which suits teams with uneven demand. Some vendors also offer flat-rate pricing for an entire organization, which can be economical for larger groups.

Popular options span a wide range. Microsoft Power BI and Google Looker Studio are low-cost or free at the entry level, with Looker Studio being especially accessible for marketing and web analytics. Tableau and Qlik are more powerful and typically cost more. Tools like Zoho Analytics, Domo, and Metabase sit in the middle, and Metabase has an open-source version you can self-host. For marketing or agency reporting specifically, products like DashThis, Whatagraph, and AgencyAnalytics charge by number of dashboards or client accounts. For finance and operations, there are specialized tools that plug into accounting systems.

When evaluating a subscription, it helps to look past the sticker price. Check which data sources connect natively, since paid connectors or API limits can add cost. Look at how many viewers you can add without extra fees, whether scheduled email delivery and exports are included, and what the data refresh limits are. Ask about annual versus monthly billing, since annual plans often save 15 to 25 percent but lock you in. Also consider the learning curve and the time your team will spend building reports, which often outweighs the license cost.

To keep spending under control, audit your subscriptions periodically for unused seats, consolidate overlapping tools, negotiate at renewal, and use free trials with a real report you actually need as the test case.

If you tell me what you're after, such as choosing a tool, comparing prices, managing existing subscriptions, or building a product that sells them, and roughly your team size and data sources, I can give much more targeted advice.

Imagine you buy a toy with your allowance, but the store clerk takes your card first and writes down the price. Later, when you say how much extra you want to give as a thank-you, that extra money gets added on. Restaurants work a bit like that.

When the server swipes your card before you add a tip, they often just take the bill amount at first. This is called a "pre-authorization" or a "hold." It is more like the bank saying "okay, this money is probably coming" than the money actually leaving your account.

Then, when you write in your tip, or when the server runs the final total, the restaurant sends the final amount to the bank. The bank then takes the full bill plus the tip out of your account or charges it to your card. Usually this happens within a day or few days, and sometimes the tip is added to the first hold so you only see one charge.

So the tip is charged after you add it, when the restaurant finishes the bill. If you ever see two charges, one for the meal and one for the tip, that just means the restaurant sent them separately, and the total you paid is still the same.

The Cambridge Computer Lab is the common name for the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge in England. It was originally founded in 1937 as the Mathematical Laboratory, and for much of its history it was known as the Computer Laboratory, a name it kept until it was formally renamed in 2017. Many people still use the older name, and the department is now based in the William Gates Building on the West Cambridge site, which it moved to in the early 2000s.

The lab has a distinguished place in the history of computing. In 1949 a team led by Maurice Wilkes built EDSAC, the Electronic Delay Storage Automatic Calculator, which is widely regarded as the first practical stored-program computer to be put into regular service. The lab also pioneered ideas such as the subroutine library, which Wilkes, David Wheeler and Stanley Gill developed to let programmers reuse code. Later work included the Cambridge Ring local area network, the Cambridge CAP computer, and contributions to operating systems, programming languages and computer security. A famous, lighter piece of its history is the Trojan Room coffee pot, which in 1991 became the first webcam when researchers pointed a camera at it so they could check whether coffee was available without leaving their desks.

Today the department is a major center for teaching and research. It offers undergraduate courses, usually as part of the Computer Science Tripos, as well as master's and doctoral programs. Research covers a broad range of areas, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, computer architecture, programming languages and formal verification, networking, security and privacy, graphics and human-computer interaction, and the use of computing in biology and medicine.

The lab also has strong ties with industry and entrepreneurship. Numerous companies have grown out of it or have research links with it, which has contributed to the so-called Silicon Fen technology cluster around Cambridge. Notable alumni and staff include Maurice Wilkes, David Wheeler, Roger Needham, Karen Spärck Jones, Ross Anderson and Andy Hopper, among many others who have shaped the field.

The sensation of air in the knee is common, but it's usually not actually air. Your knee is filled with synovial fluid, which contains dissolved gases. When the joint moves quickly or pressure changes, bubbles can form or collapse, creating a pop or cracking feeling. This is called cavitation, and by itself it's usually harmless. Many people pop their knees without any problem.

Your situation is different, though. The pop happened during a running injury, you limped afterward, and the knee still hurts when you walk and bend it. That pattern suggests a structural injury, such as a torn meniscus (the cartilage cushion inside the knee), a ligament sprain or tear, or a small piece of cartilage or bone that has shifted in the joint. Any of these can cause popping, pain, and limping, and they generally don't heal reliably with an ace bandage alone. The bandage may have eased symptoms by limiting movement, but that doesn't mean the injury has resolved.

I'd recommend seeing a doctor or physical therapist within the next few days, sooner if you notice any of the following: you can't put weight on the leg, the knee locks or catches so you can't fully straighten it, it gives way or feels unstable, there's significant swelling, or you notice warmth, redness, or fever. Those signs need prompt attention.

Until you're evaluated, avoid running and other high-impact activities, rest the knee, use ice and elevation for swelling, and only take pain relievers as directed on the label. Don't push through sharp pain when walking or bending.

If you are buying a home for the first time, securing financing can be a complicated undertaking. Several points deserve your attention when you set out to finance your first property. Start by establishing your budget: before you begin your search, you should know clearly how much you can realistically spend on a house. Take into account your income, your existing debts, and whatever savings you can put toward a down payment and closing costs. Next, look into your financing options. Homes can be financed in a number of ways, such as conventional mortgages, government-backed loans like FHA and VA loans, or alternative arrangements such as owner financing or rent-to-own contracts. Researching and comparing these choices will help you identify the one that suits your needs and financial circumstances. Getting pre-approved is another smart move, ideally before you start touring homes. Pre-approval shows you how much you are able to borrow, which helps you focus on properties within your means. It also tends to make you a stronger candidate in sellers' eyes. Keep in mind that the purchase price is not the only expense. Closing costs, property taxes, insurance, and ongoing upkeep and repairs all add up, so build these into your budget and factor them into how much home you can afford. Finally, consider working with a lender or mortgage broker. An experienced professional can explain the various loan types, guide you through the application, and work to secure the most favorable terms and interest rates for your mortgage.

Israel and the United States are home to the greatest numbers of Jewish people. The U.S. ranks second, with an estimated 7.5 million Jewish residents, equal to about 2 percent of the nation's people. Under double-entry bookkeeping, capital gains and losses are logged as either revenues or expenses, based on whether they have been realized or remain unrealized. A gain or loss is realized once the asset has been sold and the sale proceeds received; in that case it appears on the income statement as revenue (for a profit) or as an expense (for a loss). Selling a stock at a profit, for instance, would be recorded as revenue, while selling it at a loss would be recorded as an expense. When a gain or loss is unrealized, the asset has not been sold, so nothing reaches the income statement. Instead, the change in the asset's value is reflected as a change in equity on the balance sheet: a rise in the value of a stock you hold would increase equity, and a decline would reduce it. Because capital gains and losses receive different tax treatment from ordinary income, you may also need to track them separately for tax reporting. For specifics on handling them for tax purposes, consult a tax professional or review the tax rules that apply in your jurisdiction.

MyloCORT cream and Allergex Mepryamine Cream are not specifically meant to treat allergic reactions. If your mother develops a severe rash or itching while taking Risperdal, you should contact her healthcare provider right away. The provider might suggest another treatment or change her medication dose to ease her symptoms. Meanwhile, over-the-counter options such as calamine lotion or hydrocortisone cream may help soothe the itching and irritation. Using MyloCORT and Allergex Mepryamine together without first checking with a healthcare provider is not recommended, since combining them may be unsafe or unsuitable for your mother's situation. It is also essential to follow the provider's instructions and use any product exactly as directed. If her symptoms persist or get worse, contact the provider for further assessment and advice.

Artificially inflating a stock's price by trading shares with yourself at a higher figure is generally not feasible. The stock market operates under strict regulation and openness, so efforts to rig prices this way are likely to be spotted and may lead to legal trouble. A stock's price is set by supply and demand, shaped by many forces such as the company's performance and outlook, the broader economy, and how investors feel. A single investor might briefly move a price by trading a very large volume of shares, but that effect cannot be maintained over time. If your goal is to sell at a better price, the most sensible course is usually to keep your shares and wait for favorable news about the company or the market to lift the price naturally. You might also look for another buyer willing to pay more. Still, keep in mind that investing always carries risk, and the value of your holdings can rise or fall over time.

Stomach pain during urination may stem from several conditions, such as a urinary tract infection (UTI), inflammation of the bladder, or a sexually transmitted infection (STI). Other potential culprits include inflamed or irritated prostate tissue, kidney stones, and some kinds of abdominal or pelvic surgery. Urine that looks foamy may point to a problem with the kidneys or urinary tract, such as chronic kidney disease or an enlarged prostate, though it can also result from certain medications or supplements, or from eating a lot of protein. If you notice stomach pain when you urinate, you should contact a healthcare professional, particularly if the discomfort is intense or accompanied by symptoms like fever, chills, or blood in the urine. A provider can identify the underlying cause and suggest suitable treatment. Until then, drinking plenty of water, cutting back on caffeine and alcohol, and using over-the-counter pain relievers as needed may help ease your symptoms.

Eczema itself doesn't cause changes in stool. The skin condition and the digestive system are not directly linked in that way, so the eczema is unlikely to be the reason for the green color or the stringy bits. That said, a few things can be going on, and some of them are common and harmless at this age.

Green or yellowish-green stool is very common in breastfed babies. It often reflects fast transit through the gut, a bit of bile, or a change in the milk, and it can show up after a feeding change, a minor stomach bug, or simply normal variation. The white stringy bits are often mucus, which babies produce in larger amounts when they have a cold, teething-related drooling that gets swallowed, or mild irritation in the gut. Small amounts of mucus are usually nothing to worry about.

The eczema matters in one indirect way. Some babies with eczema are sensitive to cow's milk or other foods in the mother's diet (if breastfed) or in formula, and that sensitivity can sometimes show up as mucousy or greenish stools, along with skin flares. This is worth mentioning to her pediatrician rather than changing her diet on your own.

Please contact her doctor promptly if you notice any of the following: blood in the stool, stool that is very watery or frequent, signs of dehydration such as fewer wet diapers, dry mouth, or unusual sleepiness, vomiting, fever, a swollen or hard belly, or if she seems to be in pain or is feeding poorly. At seven weeks, a quick call to her pediatrician is a reasonable step even if she seems otherwise well, both to check the stool and to discuss the eczema.
