The British Empire was basically a bunch of countries and territories run by the UK government. At its peak it was the biggest and most powerful empire the world had ever seen, with land scattered across North America, South America, Africa, Asia, and Australia. It didn't happen overnight. The building started in the early 1600s and kept going well into the 1900s. Along the way Britain grabbed new territory and set up colonies all over the place. It was also a massive trading empire, and it got rich shipping stuff like cotton, tea, and spices around the world.

Then things started to unravel in the 1940s and 1950s. A lot of the places under British control wanted to run their own affairs, and Britain eventually said fine and let them go. By the 1960s most of the former territories were independent. So it took centuries to build, but it came apart pretty fast once people decided they wanted out.

Pelvic pressure is common in pregnancy and is often harmless. It can come from the baby settling lower, stretching ligaments, or your body preparing for birth. But because you're feeling immense pressure and wondering about dilation, and because preterm birth runs in your father's family, you should contact your OB or midwife today rather than waiting for your next scheduled visit. Pressure alone doesn't prove labor is starting, but a provider can check your cervix and monitor you, which is the only way to know for sure. Many offices will see you the same day for this kind of concern, and it's always appropriate to call even if you're unsure.

Go to labor and delivery or call your provider right away if you notice regular contractions or tightening (especially about every 10 minutes or more often), a dull low backache that comes and goes, cramping that feels like period pain, a change in vaginal discharge such as more fluid, mucus, or a pinkish or bloody tinge, a sudden gush or steady trickle of fluid, or if the baby seems to be moving less than usual. Don't wait to see whether these pass.

Your family history is worth mentioning to your provider. A history of preterm birth, especially in a close relative, can affect your risk and may lead to options like a cervical length ultrasound or other monitoring. Being 19 and having a second pregnancy don't prevent preterm labor, but they also don't rule it out, so it's wise to take these symptoms seriously. Most people who call with this worry turn out to be fine, and early checks are how problems get caught in time.

Radiation can cause cancer because it sometimes damages the instructions inside a cell, and a damaged cell can start growing when it shouldn't. But cancer cells are especially bad at fixing themselves, and that is the trick doctors use.

Think of each cell as a little toy factory with a rulebook. Cancer cells are like factories that have lost some of their rulebook pages, so they keep building and dividing in a messy way. When doctors aim a beam of radiation at a tumor, the beam breaks the cells' inner instructions. Cancer cells are dividing very fast, and they have a harder time repairing the breaks, so many of them die. Healthy cells can usually patch up their damage and carry on.

Doctors also don't just pick one spot and blast it once. They aim the beams from many directions so the strongest dose lands on the tumor while the nearby healthy tissue gets only a small amount. They also split the total dose into many small sessions over several weeks, which gives healthy cells time to recover between treatments while the cancer cells keep getting hit.

So the radiation is not really making new cancer. It is a strong, carefully aimed push that breaks the broken cells more than the healthy ones, and the body's own cleanup crew then removes the dead cancer cells over time.

Competitive learning is a learning rule for artificial neural networks in which a network is taught to sort inputs into categories by changing the strengths of the connections between its neurons. Under this approach, neurons vie with one another to respond to a given input. Typically, each neuron receives signals from the preceding layer, and the neuron that is activated most strongly by the input wins the contest and is the only one permitted to forward its activation onward. The connection weights are then tuned so that the network classifies inputs as effectively as possible. Competitive learning is frequently applied in self-organizing maps, which are networks trained to map high-dimensional data onto a lower-dimensional output space while retaining the data's topological structure. As a result, the network can group the data into clusters and categorize it according to how the items relate to one another. In short, competitive learning is a valuable method for teaching neural networks to classify inputs, and it is often combined with other learning algorithms to boost the network's performance.

A will is a legal document setting out how a person's property and belongings are to be divided up after they die. It may also contain directions for looking after minor children and designate a guardian to step in for them. Additionally, a will can state funeral wishes and appoint an executor responsible for putting its terms into effect. Commonly included items are: personal belongings, such as jewelry, furniture, and other household goods; real estate, such as a house or plot of land; financial holdings, such as bank accounts, stocks, and other investments; gifts and bequests, which direct particular people or organizations to receive specified items or sums; an executor, a person chosen to oversee the distribution of the estate and ensure the will's instructions are followed; and guardianship, where a parent with minor children names someone in the will to care for them should the parent be unable to. It is worth noting that a will is not the only means of passing on assets after death. Certain assets, including those held in joint tenancy or placed in a trust, may go straight to the surviving co-owner or designated beneficiary without going through a will.

You actually can, and versions of this arrangement have existed for centuries. Medieval merchants used a contract called the commenda, where one party supplied capital and another did the trading, with profits split and the investor bearing most of the losses. Today hedge funds charge a performance fee, typically around 20 percent of gains, and some private partnerships between friends or family work exactly as you describe. But several practical problems explain why it isn't the default for ordinary investors.

The biggest issue is that losses are hard to share in practice. If your manager loses half your money, he usually doesn't have the cash to reimburse you for his share, and even if he signed a contract promising to, collecting on it is difficult. So most real arrangements end up asymmetric: the manager shares in gains but not in losses. That creates a dangerous incentive, because someone who gets a cut of the upside but none of the downside is rewarded for taking big gambles with your money. Heads he wins, tails you lose.

Regulation reflects this concern. In the United States, for example, registered investment advisers generally can't charge performance-based fees to ordinary clients. Only "qualified clients" with substantial net worth may agree to them, on the theory that wealthier investors can better understand and absorb the risks. Symmetric arrangements, sometimes called fulcrum fees, where the manager's pay goes down when performance is bad, are permitted, but they're relatively uncommon because managers don't like them.

There's also a selection problem. Someone who can reliably beat the market has little reason to manage a modest account for a share of the profits; they can manage larger sums for wealthy clients or trade their own capital. The people eager to take your money on these terms are disproportionately those who are overconfident, unskilled, or dishonest. Distinguishing genuine skill from luck takes many years of track record, and evidence suggests most professional managers fail to beat simple index funds after fees.

Finally, trust and verification matter. Handing someone control of your money opens the door to fraud, hidden losses, or misreported results, which is why legitimate arrangements involve custodians, audits, and legal structures that add cost and complexity.

So the idea isn't forbidden or unworkable, but the combination of one-sided loss sharing, skewed incentives, legal limits, and the difficulty of finding a trustworthy and genuinely skilled manager makes low-cost index investing the better choice for most people.

Getting a little sore, swollen, or bruised after a blood draw is pretty common, and it usually clears up on its own in a few days. If it starts getting worse though, like more pain, more swelling, or the area turns red, or if something else just feels off to you, call your doctor or the clinic. Not always, and the strategy only makes sense under certain conditions. Paying your credit card bill late to earn a bit more savings interest is generally a bad trade, because the costs of a missed payment almost always outweigh the small interest you'd gain.

Consider the numbers. If you keep, say, $3,000 in a high-yield savings account earning 4% annually, you'd earn roughly $10 a month. Paying a few days later saves you a few dollars at most, once you account for the fraction of a month involved. Meanwhile, a late payment can trigger a fee of around $30 to $40, a penalty APR that can exceed 29% on the balance, and a hit to your credit score that can linger for years. Even one slip wipes out a lot of savings.

The smarter approach is to pay on time, every time, and ideally pay the full statement balance so you avoid interest charges entirely. If you want to capture savings interest, keep your money in a high-yield account and make sure it's there when the bill is due. You can also set up autopay for the full statement balance as a safety net, then pay manually or time things so the funds are available before the due date.

One caveat: paying a few days before the due date rather than on the due date is sensible, since payments can take time to post. But deliberately stretching payments to the edge is a gamble with little upside.

Human height is usually determined with a stadiometer, a vertical measuring device. The subject stands with their back facing the upright board, feet resting flat on the floor, and the horizontal headpiece is brought down or up until it rests on the crown of the head. The reading is taken where the lower edge of the headpiece intersects the upright board, typically recorded to the nearest millimeter or quarter inch. For an accurate result, the person must stand straight with both feet flat, and their heels, buttocks, and shoulders must make contact with the board. Shoes and any headwear, such as a hat or headband, should be taken off beforehand.

Yes, tuberculosis can affect the skin, although the lesions it causes are usually not described as tumors. Skin TB can appear as firm, painful or painless nodules, abscesses, ulcers, or sinus tracts that drain pus, and some forms, such as lupus vulgaris or scrofuloderma, can leave scarred or lumpy areas. Infections with related "atypical" mycobacteria, which are sometimes picked up from skin injuries or unusual exposures, can cause similar lesions. Many other conditions also produce lumps on the lower leg, including cysts, sarcoidosis, benign growths, and skin cancers, so the cause can't be determined from appearance alone. The key is the lab report from the removed tissue.

Your friend should first get copies of the pathology reports from every removal. Pathology reports name the diagnosis even when the patient was told only that the growths were "weird." If the reports are unclear, she can ask the surgeon or the pathology lab directly what was found. She should also ask whether the tissue was tested for mycobacteria, since a standard microscopic exam doesn't always detect TB. Specific tests include acid-fast bacilli (AFB) staining, mycobacterial culture, and PCR. If those weren't done, she can ask whether any preserved tissue blocks could still be sent for them.

Next, she should see a dermatologist, or ask her primary care doctor for a referral, and bring her full history. It's important to mention the eight years in a tuberculosis hospital, her schooling there, and her birth and upbringing in northern Germany. Doctors may order a blood test for TB exposure (an interferon-gamma release assay, or IGRA), a chest X-ray, and possibly a skin test. Keep in mind that a positive test shows exposure, not necessarily active disease, and a negative test doesn't fully rule out TB. If the tumors persist or recur, a fresh biopsy with cultures would give the most useful answer.

She should also ask her doctor about other possibilities, since a history of TB doesn't mean TB is the cause. If the growths keep coming back, or if she has fevers, weight loss, night sweats, or new lumps elsewhere, she should seek care promptly.

Your pain may be connected to your kidneys, since they sit in the lower back region. That said, lower back pain has many other possible causes, so a healthcare professional should examine you to identify the source and recommend suitable treatment. Pain from the kidneys typically shows up as a dull ache on one side of the lower back, and its intensity can be anywhere from mild to severe. Other symptoms often come with it, such as fever, trouble with urination, and pain in the abdomen. Kidney stones, kidney infections, and inflammation of the kidneys are among the conditions that can lead to this kind of pain. If you think you have kidney pain, you should see a doctor promptly so the cause can be found and properly treated. Until then, over-the-counter pain relievers and a heat source placed on the sore area may ease your discomfort. Drinking lots of fluids is also wise, because it can help wash out any kidney stones that might be responsible. Once more, a healthcare professional should be consulted for an accurate diagnosis and a treatment plan.

The name is a bit misleading, and the answer comes down to what "dividend growth" means in the fund's name versus what Yahoo Finance is showing you.

The Vanguard Dividend Growth Fund (VDIGX) is an actively managed fund that does not aim to pay a growing dividend itself. Its strategy is to buy stocks of companies that have a record of increasing their dividends and are expected to keep doing so. The "growth" refers to the underlying holdings' payout policies, not to the fund's own distributions. The fund passes through whatever dividends its holdings pay, minus expenses, and that total can rise or fall from year to year.

Several things can make the fund's own distributions look flat or erratic on Yahoo Finance. First, mutual funds typically pay distributions once or a few times a year, and the amount depends on the income the fund received, not on a steady per-share policy. Second, the fund's holdings change, and the manager may rotate into companies with lower yields but better growth, which can lower the fund's income even as each company raises its dividend. Third, the fund's expense ratio and cash flows from investors can affect net investment income per share. Fourth, Yahoo often shows only the dividend yield or recent distribution history, and distributions may include capital gains, which can be lumpy and make the dividend series look inconsistent. Also, when a fund's share price rises, the yield can fall even if the dollar amount paid per share is stable or up.

It is also worth checking whether you are looking at the right data. Yahoo's "dividend" field for mutual funds sometimes mixes income dividends with capital gain distributions, or shows only a trailing twelve-month yield. Vanguard's own site breaks out income and capital gains separately, so comparing the two is the most reliable way to see whether the income component has actually grown.

In short, the fund invests in dividend growers, but that does not guarantee that the fund's own distributions grow every year. If steadily rising income is your goal, look at the fund's per-share income distributions over several years, or consider a fund or ETF that tracks a dividend growth index, though even those do not guarantee a rising payout.

Insurance is a way of trading a small, certain cost for protection against a big, unpredictable one. You pay a company a little bit every month, and in exchange, if something bad happens that costs a lot of money, the company helps pay for it. Imagine a whole bunch of families each putting a few coins into a shared jar. Most years, nobody's car gets badly smashed, so the jar mostly sits there. But when one family's car gets wrecked and the repair costs as much as a new bicycle for everyone, the jar pays for it. Everybody gave a little so that nobody had to carry the whole bill alone.

Now, about suing the other driver. You're right that if someone crashes into you and it was their fault, they can be legally responsible for paying for the damage. The problem is that "they should pay" and "they actually pay" are two different things. Many drivers don't have much money, or don't have any insurance themselves. Suing takes months or years, costs money for lawyers and court, and you might win on paper but never collect a cent. Meanwhile, you still need a working car to get to work and take care of your family.

Your own insurance is what lets you skip that fight. You call your company, they fix your car (or pay you for it) quickly, and then the company goes after the other driver's insurance or the other driver themselves to get its money back. The hard, slow part is handled by the company, not by you.

Insurance also covers things that aren't anyone's fault, like a tree falling on your car in a storm, or a deer running into it. In those cases there's nobody to sue at all, so the shared jar is the only way the bill gets paid.

There are several routes available for purchasing government bonds issued by other countries. One option is to buy directly from the foreign government's central bank or treasury, since many governments permit both private individuals and institutions to do so. The central bank's or treasury's website usually explains the process. Another option is to work through a brokerage firm that provides international investment services, as these firms commonly let clients trade a broad range of overseas securities, government bonds included. A third option, for those who prefer not to pick individual bonds, is a mutual fund or exchange-traded fund (ETF) holding a diversified set of foreign government bonds. This offers a simple way to get exposure to overseas bond markets without the work of researching and buying each bond. No matter which approach you take, investing in foreign government bonds involves risk. If the bonds are denominated in a foreign currency, changes in exchange rates can affect your returns, and the stability and creditworthiness of the issuing government can also pose problems. Careful research and a clear understanding of these risks should come before any investment decision.

Image analysis refers to the work of pulling useful information out of pictures. It draws on methods from disciplines such as computer vision, machine learning, and data analysis in order to identify features, sort objects into categories, and study recurring patterns within images. Its uses are wide-ranging and include medicine, satellite observation, and the study of social media. For instance, in medical settings it can help spot irregularities in images like X-rays or CT scans. From satellite photos, it can reveal shifts in how land is used or in plant cover across a span of years. On social media, it can recognize and categorize the objects that appear in posted pictures. A range of approaches supports this work, among them feature extraction, object recognition, and pattern analysis, and they can be applied to all kinds of visuals, such as photographs, sketches, and maps. In short, image analysis is a valuable means of drawing out information from pictures and making sense of the data they hold.

A man can have azoospermia, a condition in which his semen contains very few sperm or none at all. Several things can cause it, such as hormone imbalances, certain illnesses, and injury to the reproductive organs. Sometimes azoospermia can be treated and fertility regained, though the available treatments and their likelihood of success depend on what is causing it. If a friend's husband has this condition, he should consult a fertility specialist or urologist to find the underlying cause and review his options. Those might include medication, surgery, or assisted reproductive methods like in vitro fertilization (IVF). When fertility cannot be restored, couples still have ways to build a family, including adoption and surrogacy. Erectile dysfunction, meaning trouble getting or keeping an erection, is also worth mentioning, since it can point to deeper health problems and deserves medical attention. It can stem from physical causes such as heart disease or from psychological ones like stress and anxiety, and it may be managed with medication, lifestyle adjustments, or therapy.

El Morro, formally Castillo San Felipe del Morro, is a 16th- and 17th-century Spanish fortress in San Juan, Puerto Rico. It sits on a rocky headland at the entrance to San Juan Bay and was built to defend the harbor and city from attacks by European rivals and pirates. Construction began in 1539 and continued for roughly two centuries, and the fort was repeatedly expanded and strengthened over that time, with its massive walls rising dramatically from the sea cliffs.

The site is part of San Juan National Historic Site, which is managed by the U.S. National Park Service and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983 along with the old city walls. Visitors can explore its bastions, dungeons, sentry boxes, tunnels, and grassy green lawn, and enjoy sweeping views of the Atlantic Ocean and the city. It is one of the most recognizable landmarks in Puerto Rico and is often pictured on postcards, tourism materials, and the Puerto Rico quarter-related imagery in popular culture.

Chest rubs such as Vicks include active ingredients that can ease coughing and cold discomfort. Once you massage the balm onto your throat, those compounds pass through the skin and enter the bloodstream. From there, they may calm swelling in the throat, which in turn can lessen the urge to cough. Additionally, the aroma of the product can open up nasal airways, making breathing more comfortable and further reducing coughing.

Purchasing a fixed deposit in India while living in Europe is feasible, though several points deserve attention first. To begin with, you need an Indian bank account, either an existing one or one you open before investing. Depending on the bank and its rules, you may be able to open it by going to a branch in person or by applying online. With the account in place, you can send money from your European bank account to your Indian one, either through your bank or through an international money transfer service. After the money arrives in the Indian account, it can be used to set up the fixed deposit.

Keep in mind that sending money abroad and investing in a fixed deposit may both involve fees, so ask your bank or financial institution about the specifics. The exchange rate between the European currency and the Indian rupee also matters, since it can change the value of your investment. Waiting for a favorable rate before you transfer funds could be advantageous. Lastly, look into the fixed deposit products offered by various Indian banks, and compare their interest rates, charges, and other conditions so you can choose the one that suits your needs best.

The men appearing in ISIS execution videos are frequently caught in an extremely perilous situation where they may have no real way out. Facing armed captors, they might believe that resisting would be hopeless, and they could worry that any effort to fight back or flee would only bring on greater brutality. Some may also have been drugged or otherwise impaired, which could cloud their judgment and limit their ability to act rationally. It's also worth keeping in mind that ISIS was a terrorist organization notorious for relying on savage violence and intimidation to maintain control. The captives may have been warned that refusing to cooperate would bring far worse outcomes. Overall, it isn't always simple to explain why people act or fail to act as they do when they are confronted with danger, so it's best to approach these situations with empathy and understanding, recognizing that people respond to stress and adversity in very different ways.

Sorry to hear about your dad's heart. There's no way for anyone to pin down the cause of his reduced heart function without a real medical workup, so his doctor is the one to ask. Lots of things can cause it, like coronary artery disease, a heart attack, valve problems, or heart failure. Treatment depends on what's going on. It might involve meds, lifestyle changes like quitting smoking, eating better, and getting regular exercise, or procedures such as angioplasty or bypass surgery. The big thing is that he sticks with what his doctor recommends and takes his meds as prescribed, since that's what really helps keep things under control and can improve how his heart works.

If you got a state tax refund last year and later repaid part of it, you might have to include the original refund amount as income on your federal return for the current tax year. The reason is that the refund may have lowered your tax bill in the earlier year, so you received a benefit that wasn't yours to keep until the following year. For that reason, the IRS counts the original refund as taxable income in the year you received it, even if you return part of it afterward. To report it, you will need to fill out Form 1040, list the refund amount under "Other income," and enter the amount you paid back as a "tax payment" on the same form. Keep in mind that this rule applies only to the original refund you received. The portion you repaid is not treated as taxable income. If you're unsure how to report the original amount of your state refund on your federal return, consider speaking with a tax professional or reading the Form 1040 instructions.

When someone passes away, their debts don't simply vanish. Instead, a court-supervised process known as probate handles the settlement of what they owed and the distribution of their property and money. As part of probate, a court names a personal representative, typically a close relative or friend of the deceased, to oversee the estate and see that outstanding debts are paid. This representative collects the deceased person's assets, pays whatever debts are owed, and passes the remaining property on to the beneficiaries named in the will or, if no will exists, to the heirs determined by state law. When the deceased left behind more debt than assets, creditors may be unable to collect everything owed and may have to treat the shortfall as a loss. Although it is unjust to shift the deceased's debts onto a spouse or children, those relatives can end up liable if they co-signed a loan or credit card account with the deceased. For this reason, people should understand their financial obligations and think carefully before agreeing to co-sign any loan or credit card.

The answer depends on which jurisdiction you mean, since tax residency rules differ widely. In the United States, for example, the federal government generally uses the "substantial presence test," which counts days of physical presence over a three-year period, so someone who spends more than 183 days in the country across the current and prior two years (with weighting for earlier years) is usually treated as a resident for tax purposes. Many U.S. states have their own rules, often based on domicile or on spending more than about 183 days in the state, and some use a "statutory resident" concept that can apply even without a permanent home. In the United Kingdom, the statutory residence test looks at days spent in the country (generally 183 days in a tax year triggers residence, with other tests involving ties such as a home, family, or work), and in Canada the test centers on residential ties and is not purely a matter of day counts. Some countries, such as Australia, use a "resides" test that considers domicile and the intention to stay, not just days present.

Because the thresholds and tie-breaking rules vary, the practical answer is that you may become a tax resident in some places in well under a year and in others never by time alone. If you have a specific country or situation in mind, tell me and I can go into its rules in more detail, though for a binding answer you should check the tax authority's guidance or consult a tax professional.

Pulmonary hypertension means the blood pressure in your lung arteries is too high. It's serious, and if it goes untreated it can lead to heart failure and other problems. Doctors often can't pin down the exact cause, but it can come from things like lung disease, heart defects, blood disorders, certain medications or substances, or genes. The usual symptoms are shortness of breath, tiredness, chest pain, and feeling lightheaded. Treatment can include medication, lifestyle changes, and sometimes surgery. If you or someone you know has this, it's really important to stay in close touch with the care team so things stay under control and nothing gets worse.

Afghan food is a mix of Middle Eastern and Central Asian flavors, and it's pretty great once you dig in. Rice is the backbone of most meals, usually served alongside whatever else is on the table. Naan is the everyday flatbread, eaten with pretty much everything. Kebabs are huge there too, usually grilled lamb or chicken, served with rice or naan. Bolani is one of my favorites: a flatbread stuffed with veggies like potato, onion, or leek, and it comes with yogurt or chutney on the side. Ashak is a bit different, with boiled dumplings packed with leeks and ground beef, topped with a yogurt sauce. Qabili palaw is the big celebration dish, rice and lamb with raisins and carrots scattered through it. Aush is a noodle soup with meat and vegetables, and it's usually served with yogurt. And the produce is amazing. Melons, grapes, pomegranates, apples, apricots, tomatoes, you name it. People use them in cooking or just snack on them straight up.

Settling your auto loan within twelve months can make sound financial sense, though the right choice depends on your personal situation. A few factors are worth weighing. First, interest: if your car loan carries a steep rate, clearing it quickly could save you considerable money, since the longer a balance lingers, the more interest accumulates. Second, financial stability: before accelerating payments, confirm that you can afford it. Using a large sum to retire the loan may leave you short on cash for other bills or unexpected costs, so maintaining an emergency fund and covering your everyday living expenses should come first. Third, other debts: if you also owe money on credit cards or student loans, it often makes more sense to tackle those first, and the general advice is to eliminate high-interest debt before low-interest debt. Fourth, opportunity cost: money used to pay off the car could instead be invested, potentially earning a greater return. In the end, the decision should reflect your own finances and goals, so it's wise to weigh the advantages and disadvantages carefully before acting.

Any physical or mental health problems that could be behind a low sex drive should be looked at first. Medications such as Manforce also deserve careful thought, since they carry possible side effects and risks. Using a drug like Manforce over the long term is generally discouraged unless a healthcare provider is involved. Manforce and other treatments for low libido, including sildenafil (Viagra), can cause side effects and are not necessarily suitable or safe for everyone. If low libido is troubling you and you are considering treatment, speaking with a healthcare provider is the right step. A provider can help identify what might be causing the problem and suggest suitable options, which could include medication, lifestyle adjustments, or counseling. It is also worth remembering that many factors can lower libido, such as physical illness, certain medications, psychological concerns, and relationship difficulties. Working with a healthcare professional can help you pinpoint the underlying cause and build a treatment plan suited to your situation.

Oregon State University's campus is in Corvallis, Oregon, which sits in the Willamette Valley out west. It's the county seat of Benton County and the biggest city in the Corvallis metro area, and that metro area covers all of Benton County. The town's pretty much built around OSU, a large public research university.

The bruise in your thigh (a pooling of blood outside the vessels) may well have resulted from the blood vessels in that area being injured when the muscle was strained. Other things can produce a hematoma as well, including physical trauma, bleeding disorders, and certain medications that interfere with clotting. Because a hematoma occasionally points to a more serious problem underneath, you should see a healthcare professional if you notice bleeding or bruising that is unusual or doesn't go away. A clinician can evaluate your symptoms and recommend the most appropriate next steps.

This sounds like a serious and urgent situation. Pus collecting along a sternal incision after open heart surgery, combined with a new high fever and body aches, may indicate a deep sternal wound infection or mediastinitis, which can spread quickly and become life-threatening. Please get him to an emergency department or call your local emergency number now rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

Until he is seen, a few things are worth doing. Keep him resting and make sure he drinks fluids if he is able. You can give acetaminophen (paracetamol) for the fever and pain if it is safe for him, but check the dose with a pharmacist or doctor first, and avoid NSAIDs such as ibuprofen unless his surgical team has approved them, since they can affect healing and kidney function. Do not try to squeeze, drain, or press on the wound yourself, and do not put anything into it. If there is a dressing, you can leave it in place unless it is soaked, and cover the area with a clean dry dressing if it is open.

Tell the staff that he had open heart surgery a few weeks ago, that he has pus from the chest incision, and that he now has a high fever and body pains. Those details will help them prioritize his care. Bring a list of his medications, any recent hospital discharge papers, and the name of his cardiac surgeon or hospital if you have it, so the surgical team can be contacted.

Treatment for this condition usually involves intravenous antibiotics, blood tests and imaging such as a CT scan to see how far the infection has spread, and often a surgical procedure to drain the collection and clean or debride the wound. Sometimes a vacuum dressing or other wound care is needed afterward. The sooner it is evaluated, the better the outcome is likely to be.

Please act on this today. If he becomes confused, very drowsy, short of breath, has chest pain that worsens, a rapid heartbeat, or faints, call emergency services immediately.

Reducing your credit limit may hurt your credit score, though how much depends on your particular situation. A few ways a lower limit could affect you are as follows. First, your credit utilization, which is the share of your available credit that you are actually using, is a factor in your score. When the limit drops, that share rises, and this can lower your score. Second, a smaller limit may restrict your ability to make big purchases with the card, which could be a problem if you depend on it for regular spending or for emergencies. Third, if any other credit accounts are tied to your card, such as a home equity line of credit, a reduced limit could also limit how much you can borrow through them. Keep in mind that these are only some of the possible effects, and the actual result for your score and finances will depend on your circumstances. If you're worried about how a lower limit might affect your credit, speaking with a financial advisor or credit counselor could help.

Think of your body like a little campfire that always makes heat. In winter, the air outside is cold, and heat slips out of you and out of your house, so we turn on the heater to make up the difference and keep you cozy. In summer, it's the opposite: the air outside is already hot, so the house gets warm on its own and we run the air conditioner to pull the heat back out.

We like it warmer in winter mostly because of how our bodies feel. When you're sitting still, your body doesn't make much heat, so a chilly room can make you shiver and feel grumpy. Warm skin, warm toes, and warm hands feel good and help you relax. In summer, we're happier with cooler air because we already feel hot and sweaty, and extra warmth just makes that worse.

Stores and offices keep it warm in winter for the same reasons. Lots of people are sitting or standing still and wearing lighter clothes indoors, so they'd feel cold without a little extra heat. Keeping people comfortable helps them work and shop, and the building is usually set to a temperature that most people find pleasant.

Chest tightness and pain radiating into the left arm can stem from many different conditions, so it's important to see a doctor if you're experiencing them. Although your symptoms may turn out to be harmless, they could also point to something serious, such as a heart attack. Several possibilities should be considered. A heart attack happens when blood supply to the heart is interrupted, damaging the heart muscle, and chest tightness along with left arm pain are common warning signs. Angina is chest pain caused by the heart receiving less oxygen than it needs; people often describe it as tightness, pressure, or a squeezing sensation in the chest, and it can also extend into the left arm. Panic attacks, which are sudden episodes of intense fear, can produce physical symptoms like chest tightness, pain, and shortness of breath, and arm pain may occur during them as well. Finally, musculoskeletal issues such as a strained muscle or a fractured rib can also cause chest tightness and pain in the left arm. Speaking with a healthcare provider is the best way to identify the cause and receive appropriate treatment, as they may order further tests or procedures to make a diagnosis. In the meantime, avoid strenuous exertion, and seek medical help right away if your symptoms worsen or if you develop any new or unusual ones.

I'm sorry you're dealing with pain in your testicles along with abdominal discomfort. Any pain that lasts or is severe deserves medical evaluation, since it may point to a condition that needs treatment. Testicular pain can stem from several sources, such as an infection, an injury, or a condition like testicular torsion or epididymitis. Torsion is a medical emergency in which the spermatic cord, the structure supplying blood to the testicle, twists. It causes intense pain and swelling, and without prompt treatment the affected testicle may be lost. Epididymitis refers to swelling of the epididymis, the tube that transports sperm away from the testicle, and it may result from a bacterial or sexually transmitted infection or other causes. Abdominal pain has many possible explanations, ranging from digestive problems and infections to conditions such as appendicitis or kidney stones. If your testicular or abdominal pain is persistent or severe, please see a doctor as soon as you can. They can identify the cause and suggest the right treatment. Until then, avoid anything that seems to trigger or worsen the discomfort, and use over-the-counter pain relievers according to the label or your pharmacist's advice.

Foamy poop can come from a bunch of things: inflammation in the gut, changes in what your intestines are producing, or just extra gas getting mixed in. If someone with pneumonia has been on antibiotics, those can shake up the gut bacteria and throw bowel movements off, which might lead to foamy stool. Dehydration, poor absorption of nutrients, and certain meds can also do it. Still, if the foamy stool keeps happening or things seem off, it's worth talking to a doctor, since they can figure out what's actually going on and what to do about it. With pneumonia especially, you'd want to make sure the infection is fully cleared and the person is eating and drinking enough.

Chest tightness after starting new medications deserves to be taken seriously, so I would not wait on this one. If the tightness is severe, is spreading to your arm, jaw, or back, or comes with shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, lightheadedness, a rapid or irregular heartbeat, swelling of your lips, face, or throat, wheezing, or hives, call emergency services right away. Those can signal a heart problem, a blood clot in the lung, or a serious allergic reaction, and none of them should be watched at home.

As for the medications themselves, chest tightness is not a typical side effect of clindamycin, but allergic reactions to antibiotics can cause chest tightness and trouble breathing, and that can happen even after a few doses. Clindamycin can also cause a pill to lodge in the esophagus and irritate it, producing a burning or tight feeling behind the breastbone, especially if taken with little water or while lying down. Oxycodone can slow breathing, which may leave you feeling short of breath or like your chest is heavy, and it can cause nausea and constipation that add to discomfort. Anxiety and pain after surgery can also produce tightness.

Another consideration is that recent surgery raises the risk of blood clots, including a pulmonary embolism, which can present as chest tightness, sharp pain with breathing, cough, or shortness of breath. That is unrelated to the drugs but important not to miss.

Because this began within a few doses and you are recovering from surgery, I would stop and get evaluated today instead of continuing to take the pills. Call your surgeon or the hospital's after-hours line now, or go to an urgent care or emergency department, particularly if the tightness is more than mild or is not clearly easing. Do not take another dose of either medication until someone has assessed you. If you do have a mild case and it seems like pill irritation, taking the clindamycin with a full glass of water and staying upright for 30 minutes afterward can help, but that is something to confirm with your care team rather than assume.

When you are seen, tell them which medications you took, when, and exactly what the tightness feels like. I hope you feel better soon, but please do get checked promptly.

Penn State's football stadium is over on the University Park campus in State College, Pennsylvania. It's called Beaver Stadium, and it holds more than 106,000 people, which makes it one of the biggest college football stadiums in the country. That's where the Nittany Lions play their home games. It sits close to other athletic facilities too, like the Bryce Jordan Center and the Penn State Ice Pavilion.

Buying a first home has financial implications that extend well beyond the purchase price, so it helps to think through the whole picture before committing.

The most obvious cost is the upfront money. Most buyers need a down payment, which is commonly around 5 to 20 percent of the price, though some loan programs allow less. On top of that come closing costs, typically 2 to 5 percent of the purchase price, covering things like loan origination fees, appraisal, title insurance, inspections, and legal or escrow fees. If your down payment is under 20 percent on a conventional loan, you will usually also pay private mortgage insurance, which adds a monthly cost until you build enough equity to have it removed. Keeping an emergency fund after closing matters too, since buying a home often drains savings and unexpected repairs arrive quickly.

The monthly commitment is the next major factor. Your mortgage payment includes principal and interest, and often property taxes and homeowners insurance, which lenders commonly collect through an escrow account. Many lenders and financial advisers suggest keeping total housing costs at or below about 28 to 30 percent of your gross monthly income, though what feels comfortable depends on your other debts and goals. Interest rates matter a great deal here. A fixed-rate mortgage gives predictable payments, while an adjustable-rate loan may start lower but can rise later.

Ongoing ownership costs are easy to underestimate. Homeowners should budget roughly 1 to 3 percent of the home's value per year for maintenance and repairs, and older homes or those with systems nearing the end of their life may need more. Utilities may be higher than in a rental, and if the property is in a community with an association, there may be monthly or annual HOA dues. Insurance and property taxes can also rise over time.

There are also longer-term financial effects. Homeownership can build equity and act as a form of forced savings, and mortgage interest may be deductible in some tax situations, though the benefit has become less common since many people now take the standard deduction. On the other hand, a home is illiquid, so selling takes time and costs money, typically including agent commissions and transaction fees. Buying also concentrates much of your wealth in one asset in one location, and home values can fall, especially in the short term.

Finally, consider the opportunity cost. Money tied up in a down payment and closing costs is no longer available for investing or other goals. Comparing the total cost of owning against the cost of renting over the time you expect to stay is a useful exercise, since transaction costs make buying more sensible when you plan to remain for several years or more.

A certified financial planner or housing counselor can help you run these numbers against your specific situation, and many first-time buyers qualify for down payment assistance programs that are worth investigating.

Teenagers are going through big changes in their bodies, and they're curious about them. Sex is also a little forbidden and a little embarrassing, so joking about it with friends feels daring. A drawing of a penis gets a laugh, a reaction, and a bit of attention from classmates, and that's a lot of what graffiti is for. Drawing something rude on a wall or desk is also a small way of pushing back against rules and adults, which many teens enjoy.

Hormones play a part too, since they make teens more interested in sex and more likely to act impulsively for a reaction. Boys are not uniquely obsessed. Many girls are just as curious, but they tend to be judged more harshly for sexual jokes or drawings, so they often keep that humor private or share it in whispers instead of on a wall.

The penis is also a simple shape that's easy to draw quickly, while female anatomy is more complicated to sketch. That may be why it shows up more often, though it isn't the main reason. Mostly it comes down to a mix of curiosity, showing off for friends, and the fact that boys are more often encouraged to joke about it openly.

Property tax is basically a tax on owning real estate. Local governments (cities, counties, school districts) rely on it to pay for things like schools, police and fire protection, roads, and other public services. Usually the bigger and more valuable the property, the more you pay. The local government sets the rate, and it gets applied to the property's assessed value. Most places assess and collect it once a year. Some governments also use it as a nudge: they might set a lower rate for certain kinds of projects, like affordable housing or commercial development, to get more of that built in the community.

It can, but it depends heavily on where you are, what kind of tax debt you have, and what type of license you're applying for. There's no single nationwide rule, so the answer varies by city, county, state, and sometimes by industry.

Many local general business licenses are fairly simple registrations, and the issuing office may never check your tax history at all. In other places, though, governments do link licensing to tax compliance. Some states and cities require a "tax clearance" certificate or check whether you owe state taxes before issuing or renewing a license, and some will deny or revoke a license if you're delinquent. This is especially common when the unpaid taxes are owed to the same jurisdiction issuing the license, such as unpaid city business taxes, local property taxes on business assets, or state sales and use taxes.

The kind of license matters too. Professional and occupational licenses, such as those for contractors, real estate agents, cosmetologists, or various health professionals, are more likely to involve tax compliance checks, and some states can suspend these licenses for unpaid state taxes. Liquor licenses, gaming licenses, and certain regulated activities often require proof that you're current on taxes. Federal tax debt owed to the IRS generally doesn't block a state or local license directly, though a federal tax lien could affect your credit, financing, or ability to get bonded, which some licenses require.

If you do owe taxes, being on a payment plan often makes a big difference. Many agencies treat a taxpayer who is in an approved installment agreement as being in good standing, so setting one up can clear the way even if you haven't paid the full balance yet.

The most reliable next step is to contact the office that issues the license you need, usually your city or county clerk or business licensing office, or your state's department of revenue or professional licensing board, and ask whether they require tax clearance. If you share your location and the type of business, I can give you a more specific idea of what to expect.

The two empires most associated with the struggle over Afghanistan were the British Empire and the Russian Empire, which competed for influence in Central Asia during the nineteenth century in a rivalry known as "The Great Game." Britain sought to protect its Indian territories from Russian expansion, while Russia sought to extend its reach southward. The contest led to the First and Second Anglo-Afghan Wars, and Afghanistan was ultimately established as a buffer state between the two powers.

So when you finance a car, the lender usually wants proof that it's insured, since the car is basically their collateral until you pay it off. If you let your coverage lapse, they can buy a policy themselves (called lender-placed or collateral protection insurance) and tack the cost onto your loan. Not fun, and it's usually way more expensive than what you'd get on your own.

Most lenders want full coverage, meaning both collision and comprehensive. Collision pays if you crash into something or roll the car. Comprehensive covers the other stuff: theft, fire, hail, falling trees, that kind of thing. Liability alone won't cut it on a financed car, even though it might be all you needed when you owned it outright.

Check your loan agreement for the exact requirements, since they can be stricter than the state minimums. Coverage limits and deductibles sometimes have specific numbers in there. If you're not sure what it says, call the lender or your insurance agent and ask. Takes five minutes and saves a headache later.

Ghost cities are places where the government and companies built lots of buildings, roads, and apartments, but very few people live there yet. The main reason is money. Local governments in China make a lot of money by selling land to builders, and they were rewarded for growing fast. So it was like a race to build big, shiny new neighborhoods, even before anyone needed them.

Builders and local governments borrowed huge amounts of money to do this. Many people also bought apartments as a safe place to keep their savings, the way you might buy a toy you hope will become more valuable. Plenty of those buyers never moved in. They just owned the apartment as an investment.

The empty part happens because people can't or don't want to move there. Many of these new cities are far from big jobs, schools, and hospitals. China also has a system called hukou, which is like a family ID that says where you're allowed to get services. A farm worker from another province may not be allowed to send their kids to good schools in the new city, so they stay where they already have access.

Nobody is actually keeping the buildings empty on purpose. It's more that the city was built for a crowd that hasn't shown up. Some places, like Kangbashi in Ordos, have slowly filled in over the years, while others are still quiet. The lesson is that building a home is easy compared to building a community where people have work and want to live.

Diplomatic immunity refers to a body of rules under which certain foreign government representatives, along with their relatives, are exempt from the laws that ordinary people must obey while they are living in another country. The reasoning is that these officials act on behalf of their home nation, and the protections let them carry out their duties without worrying that the host country might penalize them. Relatives are frequently included in this protection since they live with the official and can sometimes take part in the official's work. It is a myth that someone with diplomatic immunity can rob a bank or commit murder and escape consequences. The purpose of the immunity is to shield officials from unfair targeting or punishment by the host nation, not to give them permission to violate the law. When a person with diplomatic immunity commits a serious offense such as robbery or murder, the host country can request that the person's home country waive the immunity, which would allow the individual to be charged and punished in the host country.

Pearl Harbor is a natural inlet on Oahu, one of the Hawaiian Islands, where the Imperial Japanese Navy carried out a surprise military assault on December 7, 1941. That strike, part of World War II, was a key reason the United States joined the conflict. It marked a decisive moment in the war, with far-reaching effects for America and the wider world. In its wake, the United States declared war on Japan and became a full combatant in World War II.

Enigma was a German, Berlin-based music project created in 1990 by Michael Cretu, a Romanian-born producer and musician who was previously known for his work with Sandra, the German singer. Cretu conceived Enigma as a studio project that blended Gregorian chant and other sacred vocal elements with electronic beats, ambient textures, and downtempo rhythms, a style often described as new age meets dance music. The project's breakthrough came with its debut album, "MCMXC a.D." (1990), whose title track became a worldwide hit and helped popularize the chill-out and ambient pop sound of the early 1990s.

Enigma's identity was deliberately mysterious. Cretu rarely appeared publicly, and the project featured a rotating cast of vocalists and collaborators, most notably Sandra's former bandmate and wife, though Cretu's work at the center remained constant. The group released a series of albums over the following decades, including "The Cross of Changes," "Le Roi est mort, vive le Roi!," and "Voyageur," and had numerous hits such as "Return to Innocence," "Sadeness (Part I)," and "Sadness." Enigma became one of the best-selling electronic acts of all time, with tens of millions of records sold worldwide.

Tennessee joined the United States on June 1, 1796, becoming its 16th state. Prior to that, the land was part of North Carolina. During the late 1700s, pioneers settled the region now known as Tennessee, many of them arriving from Virginia and North Carolina. Those settlers pushed for statehood, and in 1796 Congress approved the Tennessee State Constitution, which made Tennessee the 16th member of the Union. Becoming a state follows a set sequence. A territory first petitions for statehood. Next, Congress passes legislation admitting it. Last, the president signs that legislation into law, and only then does the territory officially become a state. Tennessee went through this same process, and on June 1, 1796, President George Washington signed the act admitting it to the Union.

A computer network is a set of two or more computing devices connected to one another so they can exchange data and share resources. These devices, called nodes, can include computers, servers, smartphones, printers, routers, and other hardware. The connections between them can be physical, such as Ethernet cables or fiber-optic lines, or wireless, using technologies like Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or cellular signals.

The main purpose of a computer network is communication and resource sharing. Users on a network can send emails, transfer files, stream video, browse websites, or use a shared printer without needing a direct connection to that device. Networks also allow multiple users to access the same databases or applications hosted on a central server, which makes collaboration and centralized management far more efficient.

To work together, networked devices follow a common set of rules called protocols, which govern how data is formatted, addressed, transmitted, and received. The most widely used set is the TCP/IP suite, which underlies the internet. Each device typically has an address, such as an IP address, so that data can be routed to the correct destination.

Computer networks are often classified by their size and coverage. A local area network (LAN) connects devices within a limited area, such as a home, office, or school. A wide area network (WAN) spans a larger geographic region, sometimes across countries, and the internet is the largest example of a WAN. Other types include metropolitan area networks (MANs), which cover a city or campus, and personal area networks (PANs), which connect devices around a single person.

Prison rape is a huge problem, and it happens for a bunch of reasons. Overcrowding is a big one. When a facility is packed, guards just can't keep an eye on every corner, so things slip through. Some prisoners are also dangerous or violent, and staff may be scared to step in because they're worried about their own safety. And honestly, some guards can be bribed or bullied into looking the other way. Stopping it isn't easy, but there are things that help cut down on incidents. Cameras in key areas, more staff, and training that teaches officers to spot warning signs and act on them all make a difference.

No, dividends do not usually cause a stock's price to fall. A dividend is a cash distribution a company pays to its shareholders from its earnings. Announcing a dividend generally has little direct effect on the share price. Rather, the dividend's value tends to be built into the price before the ex-dividend date, the day on which a stock starts trading without the right to that payment. Once that date passes, the price may move to account for the fact that the dividend has been paid out and no longer belongs to the stock's value. Still, the mere payment of a dividend is not generally enough to push the price down on its own. Many other forces shape a stock's price, such as overall market conditions, economic trends, and how well the company is performing. Dividends are simply one of many factors investors weigh when deciding whether to buy or sell a given stock.

Imagine you have a toy car that can drive forward and backward on a long straight road. To describe where it is, you just need one number: how far forward or backward it is. Now imagine a flat playground instead, where the car can go left, right, forward, and back. Now you need two numbers, one for each direction. A complex number is basically a way to pack two numbers into one package, like a pair of directions that you keep together.

The "real" part tells you how far you go in one direction, and the "imaginary" part tells you how far you go in the other direction, at a right angle. The name "imaginary" is unfortunate, because these numbers are just as real as any others. People who first used them had trouble picturing them, so they gave them a spooky name that stuck.

Complex numbers are very useful because they naturally describe things that spin, wiggle, or go in circles. Turning something by a certain angle is the same as multiplying by a complex number. That's why they show up in many real-world places. Electricity in your home wall is a wave that wiggles back and forth, and engineers use complex numbers to figure out how that electricity behaves in wires and machines. Your phone and Wi-Fi send information by sending waves, and complex numbers help square up the signal so your messages arrive clearly. Doctors and scientists use them in MRI machines, which take pictures of the inside of your body. Pilots, video game makers, and the people who design bridges and airplane wings use them too, because they help describe how things move, bend, and shake.

So in short: a complex number is a two-part arrow that can point anywhere on a flat map, and that makes it perfect for describing spinning and wiggling things all around us.

Spades is a trick-taking card game played by four players in two partnerships, with partners sitting across from each other. A standard 52-card deck is used, and the suits rank from high to low as Ace, King, Queen, Jack, 10 down to 2, with spades always acting as the trump suit. Each hand begins with the dealer distributing all 52 cards so each player holds thirteen. Before any cards are played, each player looks at their hand and bids the number of tricks they expect to win, and partners add their bids together to form a team bid. A bid of zero, called a "nil," is also possible and is worth a large bonus if the player wins no tricks at all.

Once bidding is complete, the player to the left of the dealer leads the first trick by playing any card. The other players must follow suit if they can, meaning they play a card of the same suit that was led. If a player cannot follow suit, they may play any card, including a spade, which wins the trick over any card of the led suit. The highest card of the led suit wins the trick unless a spade is played, in which case the highest spade wins. The winner of each trick leads the next one. Spades cannot be led until they have been "broken," which happens when a spade has been played on a previous trick because a player could not follow suit, though some variations allow leading spades freely.

Scoring is based on whether each team meets its bid. If a team takes at least as many tricks as it bid, it earns 10 points for each trick bid plus 1 point for each extra trick, called a "bag" or "overtrick." If a team takes fewer tricks than it bid, it loses 10 points for each bid trick. Teams often track bags carefully, since accumulating ten bags typically results in a penalty of 100 points. A successful nil earns 100 points, while a failed nil costs 100 points. Play continues over multiple hands, and the first team to reach a target score, commonly 500 points, wins the game, though some groups play to 250 or other totals.

British Energy Nuclear Power Notes were not ordinary bonds or shares, so you won't find a market price for them the way you would for a listed security. They were created in early 2009 when EDF, through its acquisition vehicle Lake Acquisitions Limited, took over British Energy Group plc. Shareholders could take the standard cash offer or choose a partial alternative: a mix of cash plus Nuclear Power Notes. These notes paid annual cash amounts linked to the output of British Energy's existing nuclear fleet and to UK wholesale electricity prices over the following few years. They were generally not listed or freely tradable, so their value came entirely from the payments they generated rather than from resale.

As far as I'm aware, the notes ran for a limited period, with annual payments made over roughly 2010 to 2012, and then they were finally settled. If that's right, a note held today would normally have no remaining value in its own right. What matters is whether you or the original holder actually received all the payments due. If any went unclaimed, for example because a cheque was never cashed or the registered address was out of date, there may still be money owed.

To check, start with any paperwork you have, such as the original election form, the note certificate or statement, and any payment advices. Then contact the registrar that administered British Energy's share register and the notes, which was Lloyds TSB Registrars and is now Equiniti. Give them the holder's name, past addresses, and any shareholder reference number, and they can tell you whether payments were made or remain outstanding. EDF Energy's company secretarial or investor relations team is another possible contact if the registrar can't help. If the holder has died, the executor will usually need to provide a death certificate and grant of probate.

If you need a value for a specific date, for instance for probate or capital gains tax, the relevant figure is what the notes were worth on that date, which would reflect the payments still expected at the time. HMRC published or agreed guidance on how to apportion the base cost between the cash and the notes for those who took the alternative, so check HMRC's records or ask an accountant or tax adviser who can find the agreed apportionment figures. A probate valuation service or stockbroker experienced with unlisted and historic securities can also give you a formal valuation if needed.

Because I may not have every detail of the payment schedule exactly right, treat the registrar's records and the original offer document (the 2008/2009 scheme document for the EDF offer, often available through archived company announcements on the London Stock Exchange news service) as the authoritative sources.

A continuous function in mathematics is one with no abrupt jumps, breaks, or discontinuities. If you plotted such a function on a coordinate plane, you would get one unbroken curve with no gaps or interruptions. A function has to meet a few conditions to count as continuous. To begin with, it must be defined at every value in its domain. Next, it must have a finite limit at each point of that domain. Lastly, it should be possible to trace the graph without lifting your pencil off the paper. Continuous functions matter in mathematics and other disciplines because the tools of calculus, such as differentiation and integration, can be applied to them. Those methods allow us to examine how functions behave, determine the slopes of their graphs, and compute the areas beneath their curves. Polynomial, trigonometric, and exponential functions are typical examples of continuous functions. They appear in many applications, such as modeling real-world phenomena, solving engineering problems, and forecasting financial trends.

This is a common mistake and usually fixable, so don't panic. What you should do depends on whether the payment has already been processed and which tax agency you were paying. The guidance below assumes U.S. federal taxes paid to the IRS, though most state tax agencies and other countries' tax authorities follow a similar process.

Start by checking whether the money actually left your account. If the account number you entered doesn't exist or doesn't match the routing number, the bank will almost always reject the transaction, and the IRS will treat the payment as never having been made. If the number happened to belong to a real account that isn't yours, that bank will typically return the debit as unauthorized. Either way, your tax bill is most likely still unpaid, so watch your bank account and your IRS Online Account at irs.gov to see what the IRS has recorded.

If you scheduled the payment through IRS Direct Pay, you can usually cancel or change it online up to two business days before the scheduled payment date, using the confirmation number you received. If you scheduled an electronic funds withdrawal when you e-filed your return, you can't edit it, but you can cancel it by calling the IRS e-Pay Customer Service line at 888-353-4537 no later than two business days before the settlement date. Payments set up through EFTPS can be canceled through that system within the same window.

Once the bad payment is canceled or has failed, make a new payment with the correct information as soon as possible. You can use IRS Direct Pay with the right account, pay by debit or credit card through an IRS-approved processor (for a fee), use EFTPS, or mail a check with the appropriate voucher. Paying by the original due date prevents late-payment penalties and interest. If the deadline has already passed, paying quickly keeps those charges small.

When a payment is returned, the IRS may also send you a notice and charge a dishonored payment penalty, which is generally a small percentage of the payment or a modest flat amount for smaller payments. If that happens and the error was an honest mistake you corrected promptly, you can call the number on the notice and ask for the penalty to be removed. The IRS sometimes grants relief for reasonable cause or first-time errors. Keep records of your original confirmation, your bank statements, and your replacement payment in case you need to show what happened.

If this was a state income tax payment, contact your state's department of revenue, since cancellation procedures and deadlines vary. And if you meant the account number for receiving a refund rather than making a payment, the process is different: let me know and I can walk you through that instead.

There are a few circumstances where borrowing money may make more sense than paying with cash. When your savings aren't sufficient to cover a large purchase or a significant expense, a loan can supply the funds you need. If the interest you'd pay on a loan is lower than the gains you could earn by investing your cash instead, borrowing and investing may be a shrewd financial move. A loan that lets you buy something that produces income or gains value over time can also be a sound decision. And when a purchase or expense can't wait, a loan may be quicker and more convenient than building up the cash over time. Before committing, though, it's essential to read the loan terms closely and confirm you can comfortably manage the monthly payments. It's also wise to compare offers from several lenders to secure the best terms and interest rates.

It's wonderful that you're thinking about investing so early in life! Putting money into investments can be an effective way to build wealth over the years and move toward your financial objectives. As you get started, there are several points worth keeping in mind. First, take stock of your finances. Before investing, you should have a clear picture of where you stand, which means setting aside an emergency fund for surprise costs, paying down any debt that carries high interest, and defining specific financial goals. Second, learn the basics. Investing can feel daunting when you're new to it, so spend time understanding the various options available and the risks and returns that come with each. Books, articles, online courses, or a conversation with a financial advisor can all help you grasp the fundamentals. Third, begin modestly. There's nothing wrong with starting with small amounts and increasing them gradually. Some people invest a fixed sum each month using dollar-cost averaging, a method that can soften the impact of market swings and lower the risk of committing a large amount all at once. Fourth, spread your holdings across different types of assets. Diversification means distributing your money among categories such as stocks, bonds, and cash, which helps limit the damage if one category underperforms. In short, patience and a long-term outlook matter a great deal in investing. It's also wise to revisit your strategy from time to time and adjust it as your circumstances and goals change. Finally, before making any major investment decisions, consider consulting a financial advisor or professional, who can build a plan tailored to your specific situation and objectives.

RFID tags get their power in a few different ways. Passive tags have no power source of their own. They wake up when the reader sends out radio frequency energy, and that energy powers the chip so it can send its stored data back. Active tags carry their own power, usually a small battery, which runs the chip and handles the transmitting. Semi-passive tags sit somewhere in between: they have a small battery that keeps the chip running, but they still rely on the reader's signal to respond. The reader's energy boosts the signal coming back from the chip, so it can be picked up from farther away. Which kind you need really comes down to what you're using it for.

Chest pain and dizziness may stem from a wide range of causes, so anyone experiencing them should seek medical care, since they can point to a serious underlying condition. Among the possibilities are heart-related problems, such as angina, a heart attack, or an irregular heartbeat known as a cardiac arrhythmia. These symptoms can also occur during a panic attack, a sudden surge of intense fear or anxiety. Acid reflux, where stomach acid moves upward into the esophagus, is another potential cause. A pulmonary embolism, which is a blockage in the pulmonary artery, can likewise produce chest pain and dizziness. Finally, dizziness alone may come from inner ear disorders like vertigo. Again, seeing a healthcare provider is important when chest pain and dizziness occur, because they may signal a serious problem. A provider can identify the source of the symptoms and recommend suitable treatment.

Erytop cream is a topical med with erythromycin in it, an antibiotic. People use it for acne and some other skin infections. It can help cut down on pimples, but you really want to use it the way your doctor or the product label says. If you're putting it on at night, just make sure you wash it off in the morning. Leaving it on all day and night can raise the odds of irritation or dryness. A gentle cleanser in the morning helps too, so your face doesn't get stripped.

Beyond the cream, a few things can make a difference. Wash your face twice a day with a gentle, oil-free cleanser, and skip the scrubbing since that just irritates things and can make breakouts worse. Try not to pick or squeeze pimples, because that's how you end up with scars and more redness. Pick a moisturizer made for acne-prone skin that won't clog pores. Go for oil-free makeup and hair products, and look for "non-comedogenic" or "oil-free" on the label. Eating well, with plenty of fruit, veggies, and healthy fats, may help your skin too.

If you're unsure about your skin or how the treatment is going, check in with a doctor or dermatologist. They can tell you what makes sense for your situation and history.

A language model is a statistical tool that estimates how probable a given sequence of words is. It assigns a probability to a word sequence, reflecting how likely that sequence is to appear in a particular context. These models power many natural language processing applications, including speech recognition, machine translation, and text generation. Several varieties exist, among them character-based, word-based, and n-gram models. A character-based model estimates the probability of a string of characters, whereas a word-based model does the same for words. An n-gram model estimates the chance of each word in a sequence by looking only at the preceding n-1 words. Such models can be fitted to large collections of text using methods like maximum likelihood estimation or neural networks. Training aims to capture the statistical regularities and connections present in a language, enabling the model to predict accurately how likely different word sequences are.

I'm sorry you're dealing with this. Testicular pain with a lump, a pulling-down sensation, and abdominal discomfort is worth having checked promptly, ideally within the next day or so rather than waiting to see if it passes.

Several things could cause these symptoms. The most common are an epididymitis (inflammation of the tube behind the testicle, often from an infection), or a hernia, such as an inguinal hernia, where part of the intestine pushes through a weak spot in the lower abdominal wall into the groin and scrotum. A hernia fits well with what you describe: discomfort when standing or walking, relief when lying down, a pulling feeling, and pain that can extend into the abdomen. Less commonly, a testicular torsion (a twisted testicle) can cause similar symptoms, and it is an emergency because the blood supply can be lost within hours. Any lump in the testicle itself also needs to be evaluated, since although most lumps are benign, a doctor should confirm what it is.

Please go to an emergency department or urgent care right away if you have sudden or severe pain, pain that comes on quickly, nausea or vomiting, fever, swelling that is getting bigger, skin redness or warmth, a testicle that sits higher or at an odd angle, or if the abdominal pain becomes severe, or if you cannot pass gas or stool or have a bulge that becomes hard and painful. These can signal torsion or a trapped hernia, which need urgent treatment.

If none of those apply, book an appointment with your doctor in the next day or two, or see a urologist or a general practitioner. Tell them exactly what you told me, including when the lump appeared and how the pain changes with position. Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous activity until you have been examined, and wear supportive underwear if it helps. Do not try to push on the lump or treat it yourself with strong painkillers before being seen, since that can hide важные signs.

A test, which is sometimes called an assessment, is a way of judging a person's or a group's knowledge, abilities, talent, physical condition, or category. Educators, professional certifying bodies, psychologists, and military organizations frequently rely on tests to gauge how well someone performs or to pinpoint where further development is needed. Tests may take many forms, such as written exams, spoken interviews, or hands-on demonstrations, and they can target a broad spectrum of capabilities, including mastery of a specific field, the capacity to solve problems, or bodily fitness. Test outcomes may guide choices about whether a person is a good fit for a given position, training program, or academic path.

The U.S. Constitution was written during the Constitutional Convention, which met in Philadelphia from May 25 to September 17, 1787. Delegates from twelve of the thirteen states (Rhode Island declined to send anyone) drafted the document, and it was signed on September 17, 1787. It then had to be ratified by at least nine states, a process that was completed in 1788, and it took effect in March 1789.
