The Berlin Blockade was a diplomatic and military standoff lasting from 1948 to 1949. It stands as a significant episode of the early Cold War and marked a decisive turning point in relations between the Western powers and the Soviet Union. The roots of the crisis reach back to the close of World War II in 1945. Once the war ended, the Allied powers, namely the United States, the United Kingdom, and the Soviet Union, split Germany into four occupation zones, and Berlin, the capital, was likewise carved into four sectors. At first, the Western powers and the Soviet Union worked together to govern Germany and Berlin, but as they disagreed over how the country should be rebuilt and ruled, friction grew. Reparations were one major point of contention: the Soviet Union pressed for heavy payments from Germany, whereas the Western powers resisted. The Soviet Union also rejected the Marshall Plan, a postwar program designed to revive Western Europe, Germany included. Moscow viewed the plan as a Western effort to extend its economic and political control over Europe. Reunification was another source of discord. The Western powers favored bringing Germany back together as one state, but the Soviet Union opposed this, fearing that a unified Germany, given its record of aggression and expansion, would pose a threat to Soviet security. Together, these disputes fostered growing distrust and hostility between the Western powers and the Soviet Union, and ultimately produced the Berlin Blockade.

Porcupines are plant eaters, pretty much through and through. In the wild they mostly munch on tree bark, twigs, and other plant stuff. Inner bark is their favorite. They chew through the tough outer layer to get at it, which is a lot of work, but they seem to think it's worth it. Leaves, shoots, and nuts show up on the menu too, depending on what's growing around them.

They'll eat a huge range of trees. Pine, spruce, and fir are common targets, and so are hardwoods like oak, maple, and beech. Fruit trees are fair game as well. Apple and pear bark and shoots are big draws, which is why orchard owners aren't always thrilled to see them.

Now and then a porcupine might snack on a bug or a bit of something small, but that's really just an occasional extra and not a real part of their diet. They're not hunters. They don't chase down other animals, and they're generally pretty chill unless they get cornered.

It's pretty common for a stock to hit one big peak, or have a stretch of strong performance, and then slide back down. Lots of things can cause that: shifting market conditions, how the company is actually doing, or just how investors feel about it. Say a company posts great earnings or launches a hot new product. The stock can jump, but if the company can't keep that momentum going, the price often drifts back down. Sometimes a stock spikes because of speculation or hype, and when the company fails to live up to what people expected, the bubble pops. That's why it pays to dig into the fundamentals and think about the risks before buying into a particular stock. Doing that homework won't guarantee you never get burned, but it helps you make smarter calls and keep your losses in check.

Cluster analysis is basically a way of sorting data points into groups, or clusters, based on how similar they are. The whole idea is that points in the same group should look more like each other than like points in other groups. There isn't just one way to do it, though. The best method depends on your data and what you're trying to find out. Some popular ones are hierarchical clustering, k-means, and density-based clustering.

Hierarchical clustering builds a sort of family tree of clusters, with smaller clusters nested inside bigger ones. It starts by treating every point as its own cluster, then keeps merging the two closest clusters until everything is linked together in one hierarchy.

K-means is probably the one people run into first. You pick k, the number of clusters you want, and the algorithm drops k starting centroids somewhere (usually at random). Each point gets assigned to whichever centroid is nearest, the centroids get moved to the middle of their new groups, and you repeat that until nothing changes much anymore.

Density-based clustering takes a different angle. Instead of picking a number of clusters, it looks for dense crowds of points and treats each crowd as a cluster. Anything sitting alone in sparse areas gets labeled as noise or outliers. It's handy when your clusters have weird shapes that k-means would butcher.

People use this stuff all the time to poke around in data and spot patterns. Market segmentation, image analysis, and gene expression work are all common examples.

Imagine you have a big box of toy fish, and the lakes are like bathtubs scattered all over the world. Fish live in bathtubs, but bathtubs aren't connected by pipes, so how did the same kind of fish get into so many of them?

Here are the main ways it happened:

Long ago, the lakes were connected. Millions of years ago, the land was different. Rivers flowed into each other, and lakes sometimes joined up. Fish could swim from one place to another, and then slowly the land shifted and cut them apart. The fish that got left in each bathtub stayed there and changed a little over time.

Ice helped too. During the Ice Ages, huge sheets of ice covered much of the north. Water from melting ice formed new rivers and lakes that linked up in new ways, so fish could slip from one watershed into another. When the ice melted, new waterways opened and closed.

Some fish got carried by birds. A fish egg or a tiny fish can stick to a bird's feet or feathers, or get swallowed by a bird and dropped in a new pond. Birds fly long distances, so this is a surprisingly good way to hop between lakes.

Some fish got carried by people. People have moved fish on purpose, to have more to catch, and by accident, in buckets or boats. Northern Pike are famous sport fish, so people have stocked them in many lakes.

Northern Pike are a good example. Their ancestors probably lived in connected waters across the cold north long ago. When the land and ice changed, their groups got split, and some got carried by water, birds, and people to new lakes. Over time, the pike in each lake became a little different, but they're still the same kind of fish.

IQ, short for intelligence quotient, is a gauge of how smart a person is. It comes from a standardized test that assesses mental skills like solving problems and thinking critically. Some individuals hold that IQ scores differ among racial groups and that genetic distinctions between those groups account for the gap. That view is mistaken. No scientific evidence shows that race determines IQ. Many researchers instead point to a range of influences on IQ, such as surroundings, schooling, and life experiences. Intelligence is also not set in stone: people can sharpen their minds and cognitive abilities through learning and experience, whatever their race. Therefore, it is wrong to conclude that a person's race dictates their IQ.

Rock of Ages is a rock musical about Sherrie Christian, a young singer and actress who arrives in Hollywood in 1987 hoping to make it big. She takes a job at the legendary rock venue The Bourbon Room, where she falls for Drew Boley, a bartender with ambitions of becoming a rock star. As the two build their relationship amid the ups and downs of the Hollywood music world, their future is put at risk by German developer Hertz Klinemann, who plans to tear down The Bourbon Room and replace it with a shopping mall. The show is packed with 1980s classic rock tunes, including songs made famous by Journey, Bon Jovi, and Def Leppard.

Major moves in the foreign exchange market are usually driven by events that change expectations about interest rates, economic growth, or political stability. Central bank decisions are among the most powerful. When the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, Bank of Japan, or Bank of England raises or cuts interest rates, or signals a change in direction, capital tends to flow toward currencies offering higher returns, and the currency can move sharply within minutes. Monetary policy meetings, press conferences, and the forward guidance that accompanies them often matter as much as the rate decision itself.

Macroeconomic data releases also trigger large swings. Inflation reports such as the consumer price index, employment figures like the U.S. nonfarm payrolls report, GDP growth numbers, retail sales, and purchasing managers' indices all shape views about where interest rates are headed. A figure that comes in far above or below forecasts can reprice currencies almost immediately.

Geopolitical shocks and crises produce sudden moves as well. Wars, terrorist attacks, coups, sovereign debt concerns, and banking failures often send investors toward perceived safe havens such as the U.S. dollar, Swiss franc, and Japanese yen, while weakening currencies of countries seen as riskier. Elections and referendums can have similar effects, as the Brexit vote in 2016 demonstrated with a sharp fall in the pound.

Commodity prices matter particularly for currencies of resource-exporting nations. Movements in oil affect the Canadian dollar, Norwegian krone, and Russian ruble, while gold and other metals influence currencies such as the Australian dollar and South African rand.

Finally, government intervention and policy surprises can jolt markets. Central banks sometimes intervene directly to buy or sell their currency, as Japan has done to support the yen, and sudden capital controls, unexpected policy announcements, or shifts in trade policy such as new tariffs can likewise trigger rapid repricing.

If your 401(k) account seems to be missing dividend payments, several explanations are possible. You can work through the problem with the following steps. Start by contacting your employer or your 401(k) plan administrator to find out whether dividend distributions have been held up, since a processing problem could be the cause. Next, confirm that your account holds the right investments. Stocks and mutual funds are the usual sources of dividends, so if your money is not in these kinds of assets, you may simply not be receiving any. Review your account statements as well to see whether the dividends were posted. When they were not, the cause could lie with the investment itself or with how the payments are being distributed. If the problem persists, consider speaking with a financial advisor or a representative of your plan administrator, who may be able to resolve it. Keeping careful records of your dividends and any other income from your 401(k) matters, because it affects your overall financial picture and retirement planning. For concerns about missing dividends or any other questions about your account, a financial professional or your employer can offer useful guidance.

Crocodiles live in tropical and subtropical regions across the world. They are found in parts of Africa, Asia, Australia, the Americas, and the Caribbean. Their habitats include rivers, lakes, swamps, marshes, estuaries, and mangrove coastlines. Saltwater crocodiles, the largest species, can even swim far out into the ocean and inhabit brackish or salty coastal waters, while many other species prefer freshwater environments. Because they are cold-blooded, they depend on warm climates and often bask on riverbanks or mudflats to regulate their body temperature.

Yoshua Bengio is a computer scientist and professor at the University of Montreal, and he's one of the big names in deep learning. That's the branch of AI where neural networks learn from data and make decisions on their own. He's done a lot of work on artificial neural networks, natural language processing, and machine learning more broadly. In 2018 he shared the Turing Award with Yann LeCun and Geoffrey Hinton for their deep learning work. People often call the Turing Award the "Nobel Prize of Computing," and it goes to folks who've made major contributions to computer science.

Therapy can really help with stiffness and hand function after a stroke, though how much depends on a bunch of things: how bad the stroke was, where it hit, how long ago it happened, and his overall health. The best next step is to get him in front of a physical or occupational therapist who can look at what he can do now and build a plan around his specific goals. Recovery is usually a slow, grinding process, so don't be surprised if progress comes in small steps. Those little wins still matter a lot for daily life, so it helps to stay patient and keep encouraging him.

Flank pain, the area on the sides of the back just below the ribs, has many possible causes, and since your urine, bloodwork, and X-rays were normal, some of the more urgent ones are less likely. Here is a general overview to help you prepare.

Musculoskeletal causes are among the most common, especially when pain is dull and on both sides. Strained muscles from exercise, lifting, or even prolonged sitting with poor posture can do this. Problems in the lower thoracic or upper lumbar spine, such as joint irritation, a mildly irritated nerve, or arthritis, can also refer pain to the flanks. Rib or costovertebral joint dysfunction, where the ribs attach to the spine, is another frequent culprit. These often feel worse with movement, twisting, deep breaths, or pressing on the area, and X-rays can look normal.

Kidney-related causes are what most people worry about. Kidney stones, infections, and blockages typically cause pain on one side, often severe and coming in waves, and usually show blood or infection signs in urine. Your normal urine and bloodwork make these less likely, though a small stone or early problem is not completely excluded, and plain X-rays miss many stones. A CT scan or ultrasound is the usual next step if suspicion remains. Pain on both sides can occasionally come from conditions affecting both kidneys, but those usually show up in blood or urine tests.

Digestive causes can also refer pain to the back and flanks. Constipation, gas, irritable bowel, gallbladder or pancreas problems, and acid-related issues can all do this. Upper abdominal organs sit close to this region, so it is worth noting any link to meals, bowel habits, bloating, or nausea.

Other possibilities include shingles, which causes burning pain before a rash appears, and in women, gynecologic conditions. Dehydration, stress, and muscle tension can contribute too. Less commonly, lung-related problems like irritation of the lining around the lungs can cause pain below the ribs, especially if it changes with breathing.

To make your appointment more productive, consider noting when the pain started, whether it is constant or comes and goes, and what makes it better or worse, such as movement, position, eating, urinating, or deep breathing. Mention any recent injury, new exercise, or heavy lifting, plus changes in bowel habits, appetite, weight, or any fever, rash, or urinary symptoms. Bring a list of medications and supplements, including anti-inflammatories, which can affect the kidneys and stomach.

Seek care promptly if you develop fever, severe or sudden worsening pain, blood in the urine, vomiting, trouble urinating, leg weakness or numbness, shortness of breath, or chest pain. Otherwise, your doctor can do a physical exam, which often distinguishes muscular from organ-related pain, and decide whether imaging like an ultrasound or CT is warranted.

Swelling of the foreskin accompanied by red patches after sex can have several different causes, so it is important to see a healthcare provider who can identify the exact problem and recommend the right treatment. Among the likely explanations are sexually transmitted infections (STIs), allergic reactions, and irritation or inflammation. Infections such as gonorrhea, chlamydia, and syphilis can make the foreskin and penis swell and turn red, and they often cause burning during urination. Herpes can also lead to redness and swelling, along with blister-like sores on the foreskin or in the surrounding genital area. Allergies to condoms, lubricants, or other products used during intercourse may produce similar swelling and redness, often with itching and a burning sensation. Inflammation of the foreskin, called balanitis, is another possibility and may result from poor hygiene, snug clothing, or contact with certain chemicals. A yeast infection could also be responsible, causing swelling, redness, itching, and burning. Yeast infections occur when the Candida fungus grows out of control and are typically treated with antifungal medication. Because these conditions have such overlapping symptoms, a healthcare provider's evaluation is essential to pinpoint the cause and begin appropriate care.

Using a credit card convenience check can be handy when you need to pay for something or get some cash fast, but it's worth knowing the downsides before you write one. Here's what to think about.

First, the cost. Convenience checks usually carry higher interest rates and fees than regular card purchases, so read the terms carefully and figure out what it'll actually cost you before you cash one.

Second, your credit utilization. Writing a check adds to your balance, which raises the share of your available credit you're using. That can drag down your credit score, so keep an eye on it.

Third, fraud. These checks look like regular checks, so if they get stolen, someone else can cash them and run up your account. Store them somewhere secure and don't leave them lying around the house or in the car.

Last, look at other options. Pulling from a savings account or taking out a personal loan might be cheaper. It's worth comparing before you commit.

So weigh the pros and cons, and be careful about the costs and risks.

On Facebook, a tag lets you mention another user or a page within a post, comment, or message. Tagging someone creates a link to their profile, and that post or comment becomes visible to them and their friends. People and pages can be tagged in posts, photos, and other kinds of content. To do so, type the "@" symbol followed by a person's name, then pick them from the list of suggestions that appears. Pages work the same way: type "@" followed by the page's name. Tags are a helpful way to call attention to a person or thing in a post and can make the post or comment easier to find. Whoever you tag receives a notification, which can boost engagement and bring more traffic to the post. Even so, tags should be used thoughtfully, applied only when they are relevant and suitable.

Imagine a big playground with a very strict head teacher and lots of helpers. China calls itself a communist country, which means the government says it works for everyone, and the one group in charge is the Chinese Communist Party. The Party is like the team that makes all the big rules. It has a leader at the top, a smaller group of important people who help decide things, and then many, many members spread across the country in towns, cities, schools, and workplaces. Elections for the top jobs aren't free the way they are in many countries, so the Party picks its own leaders instead of ordinary people voting for them directly. There is a government too, with officials who run things like roads and schools, but the Party sits above it and makes sure those officials follow its plans.

As for watching what people say, think of a huge telephone game where some grown-ups stand in the middle listening. The government uses computer programs that scan messages on phones and websites, looking for certain words or topics it doesn't like, such as criticism of leaders or news about protests. When the computers spot something, the post can be deleted or the account can be shut off for a while. Companies that run apps and websites in China are required by law to follow these rules, so they do much of the checking themselves, and many employ large teams of people to read posts too. Some websites from other countries, like many well-known social media and search sites, are blocked altogether, which is why people inside China often use a special tool called a VPN to reach them, though that is also against the rules and can be risky.

There is also a rule that people who post things the government considers troublemaking can get in trouble with the police, and sometimes they are punished for it. Because of this, many people choose to be careful about what they say, even when they aren't sure exactly where the line is. That fear of getting in trouble is part of what makes the system work, because people police themselves as well.

A "loaded" word is a word that carries more than its plain meaning. Imagine a word is like a backpack. Some words just hold what they say, like "table" or "rain." But a loaded word also packs extra feelings, opinions, or hints inside it, so when someone uses it, they are often nudging you to feel a certain way about the thing they're talking about.

For example, imagine two people describing the same group of protesters. One calls them "passionate" and the other calls them "rowdy." Both words could describe the same people, but "passionate" sounds admiring and "rowdy" sounds negative. Those extra feelings packed inside the words are the "load," and that is why people say the word is loaded.

So when you hear someone say a word is loaded, they mean the word is doing some quiet persuading or signaling beyond just pointing at the thing itself. It's a bit like a sticker on a box that tells you what to think of what's inside before you open it.

A hard fall onto your buttocks sends a lot of force up through your pelvis and spine, and your body usually reacts by violently tensing your core muscles at the moment of impact. Because your pain shows up mainly when you sit up, get up from lying down, or shift into certain positions, the most likely explanation is a strained or pulled abdominal muscle. The rectus abdominis (the "six-pack" muscle) and the obliques along your sides do most of the work when you rise from lying or sitting, so a strain there typically causes sharp pain with exactly those movements and feels better when you're still. Being yanked down by your friend could also have twisted your torso as you fell, which makes an oblique strain even more plausible.

Another possibility is a bruised or irritated rib, or inflammation where the ribs meet the cartilage at the front of your chest (costochondritis). That kind of injury causes sharp pain when lying in certain positions, twisting, or taking a deep breath, and the area is often tender if you press on it. Even if you didn't hit your ribs directly, the jolt and the bracing can sometimes irritate these areas. Muscle strains and minor rib injuries usually improve over one to a few weeks with rest, avoiding heavy lifting and strenuous core exercise, gentle movement, ice or heat, and over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen if they're safe for you. A helpful trick for getting up is to roll onto your side first and push yourself up with your arms so your abdominal muscles don't have to do the work.

A fall can occasionally cause internal injury, though, so it's worth getting checked by a doctor, especially since the pain has lasted several days. Go to an emergency room promptly if you notice any of these: pain that is getting worse instead of better, pain that's constant even at rest, a swollen, rigid, or very tender belly, nausea or vomiting, blood in your urine or stool, dark or tarry stools, dizziness or fainting, shortness of breath or pain with every breath, fever, or pain spreading to your shoulder (which can be a sign of internal bleeding). Pain in the left upper abdomen deserves extra caution because the spleen sits there and can be injured in falls.

If none of those warning signs are present and the pain is clearly tied to movement and slowly easing, a muscle strain is the most likely culprit. Still, a quick visit to a doctor or urgent care can confirm that with a simple exam and give you peace of mind.

You can usually find the full book of bids and asks on a stock exchange itself, or through your brokerage's platform. On the exchange side, it's called an "order book," and it lists every outstanding order for a given stock, with the price of each bid or ask and how many shares are being offered at that price.

If you've got a brokerage account, you can probably pull up the whole book in their trading platform or on their website. Some brokers also offer real-time streaming quotes, which show the bids and asks along with the latest trade price and volume.

One thing to keep in mind is that all this stuff moves fast. Orders get placed, canceled, and filled constantly, so what you're looking at might already be a little stale or incomplete by the time you read it.

Sesame seeds are those tiny, oily seeds that come from the sesame plant, which originally comes from tropical parts of Africa and Asia. The plant's an annual herb, and it puts out clusters of small, fragrant flowers. Once those are done, the seeds start to develop. You'll find them in tons of cuisines around the world, usually as a condiment or a spice, or just tossed into all kinds of dishes. They're also pressed for oil, which people cook with, but it ends up in stuff like soaps and cosmetics too.

Probabilistic reasoning is a way of thinking that accounts for how likely different outcomes or events are. Drawing on probability theory and statistical methods, it lets people form predictions, make decisions, and draw conclusions from information that is uncertain or incomplete. It can be applied to forecast how likely future events are, to assess the risks tied to various courses of action, and to choose wisely when the outcome is unknown. Disciplines such as economics, finance, engineering, and both the natural and social sciences rely on it frequently. At its core, it works with probabilities, numerical values expressing how likely an event is to happen. A probability runs from 0, meaning the event cannot happen, up to 1, meaning it is guaranteed. These values may also be written as percentages or fractions. The reasoning might concern the chance of one event, the joint chance of several events happening together or one after another, or the chance of an event given that another has already taken place. Because so many real-world situations contain uncertainty and variation, probabilistic reasoning is a valuable tool for making sound decisions and for making sense of the world.

Sears Holdings, the parent company of Sears and Kmart, has been in financial trouble for years and could end up going under. There are a few big reasons. First off, retail is brutally competitive. Sears used to be the place to shop, but now you've got Walmart, Target, and plenty of others selling similar stuff, often cheaper or with a wider selection. That makes it tough to pull people in. Second, Sears has struggled to keep up with how people shop now. Back in the day everyone went to physical stores, but these days a lot of folks just order online, and Sears never really caught up with that shift. Third, the money side is a mess. The company carries a huge pile of debt, so a lot of its cash goes to paying people back instead of running the business. That makes it hard to invest in stores, update the website, or just keep the lights on. So it's a mix of tough competition, slow adaptation, and debt that's squeezing them from every direction.

Okay, so the Truth-in-Lending Disclosure is a document lenders have to give you when you take out a loan. It's meant to spell out the key terms in plain numbers: the APR, the finance charge, and the total amount of the loan. To work out the APR, you'd need the interest rate, how many payments you'll make over the life of the loan, the amount of each payment, and any fees tacked on, like origination fees or closing costs.

The finance charge uses the same pieces: the interest rate, the number of payments, the payment amount, and those extra fees or charges.

The total amount of the loan is simpler. You just need the principal (what you're borrowing) and the finance charge you just calculated.

There are plenty of formulas and methods for these numbers. If you've got a financial calculator or a spreadsheet program, you can run them yourself. Otherwise, an online calculator works, or you can ask a financial professional to check your math. Either way, read through your loan terms carefully. It's the best way to make sure you actually know what you're signing up for.

If you mean the British car brand, the answer is none, since no Land Rover vehicle has ever been sent to Mars. If you mean robotic rovers that have landed on the Martian surface, there have been six successful ones, plus one more that arrived but never got to work.

NASA has landed five of them. Sojourner arrived with the Mars Pathfinder mission in 1997 and was a small, microwave-sized rover. Spirit and Opportunity, twin rovers, landed in early 2004, and Opportunity famously kept operating until 2018, far beyond its planned 90-day mission. Curiosity landed in 2012 and is still active, as is Perseverance, which landed in 2021 and carried the Ingenuity helicopter. China added a sixth when its Zhurong rover landed in May 2021 as part of the Tianwen-1 mission, operating for about a year before going dormant.

The Soviet Union's Mars 3 lander touched down in 1971 carrying a small tethered rover called PrOP-M, but contact was lost seconds after landing, so the rover never deployed. An identical rover aboard Mars 2 was destroyed when that lander crashed earlier the same year.

Honestly, you usually can't lock in a mortgage rate years ahead. Rates move pretty much every day based on the economy, market conditions, and what it costs lenders to get money. If you're thinking about buying in the next five years, the smart move is to get ready now: clean up your credit score, start saving for a down payment, and read up on the different loan types and rates out there. Talking to a lender or a financial advisor can help too. They can tell you where the market is headed (as far as anyone can tell) and what you can do to put yourself in a good spot when you finally apply.

Once you're actually applying, you can usually lock a rate at that point, or when you sign the mortgage agreement. That protects you if rates jump before closing. Just keep in mind that locks often cost money, and the rate you get might not be the lowest one floating around that week.

Clint Walker was an American actor who became widely known for playing the lead character in the Western TV series "Cheyenne," which aired during the 1950s. Born Norman Eugene Walker on May 30, 1927, in Hartford, Illinois, he started out as a contract performer at Warner Bros. during that decade. Over the course of his career, he acted in numerous movies, among them "The Ten Commandments," "The Dirty Dozen," and "The Great White Hope," and he also made guest appearances on television programs like "The Love Boat" and "The A-Team." In addition, he recorded music and released several albums with a Western theme. Walker died on May 21, 2018, at 90 years old.

The tectonic plates are believed to make up the lithosphere, the rigid outermost layer of the Earth. This layer includes the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle, and it sits atop the more ductile asthenosphere, which allows the plates to slowly move over it.

It sounds like you've been diagnosed with hepatitis C, a viral infection that can inflame and damage the liver. The HCV test is what confirms the diagnosis. The stiffness test (also called the AST test, for aspartate transaminase) measures a liver enzyme in your blood, and high AST levels can point to liver damage. Treatment usually means antiviral meds to clear the virus. They work really well for most people, but they aren't right for everyone. Your doctor will look at your overall health and which strain you have before picking a plan.

If you're looking into treatment in India, talk to a qualified provider who can walk you through your options. Ask about cost and availability too, plus side effects and risks. Stick with whatever your doctor tells you and take the meds exactly as prescribed. Also, try to protect your liver: cut back on alcohol and anything else that's hard on it, and get vaccinated for hepatitis A and B if you haven't already. Hope this helps, and feel free to ask if anything's still unclear.

So it really depends on who's holding the shares and what kind of shares they are. That said, a few things come up a lot.

If you sell shares you've held for more than a year, your profit counts as a long-term capital gain and usually gets taxed at a lower rate than regular income. Sell within a year or less and it's a short-term gain, which gets taxed at your ordinary income rate, so it can hurt more.

Dividends are usually taxed as ordinary income at your marginal rate. Nothing fancy there, but it catches people off guard.

Employee stock options are where things get messy. It depends on whether they're qualified or non-qualified. With qualified options, you generally get taxed when you exercise. With non-qualified ones, the hit usually comes when you sell the shares. The rules here can get pretty tangled, so if you've got a real stake in this, talk to a tax pro or check the IRS site.

I'm sorry your partner is unwell. A rash that appears after starting a new medicine, especially alongside nausea, sweating and feeling faint, could be a drug reaction. Co-codamol contains codeine and paracetamol, and either can cause side effects. Nausea, sweating and light-headedness are common with codeine, and itching and rash can also occur. An allergic reaction is less likely but possible, so it is worth taking seriously.

First, he should stop taking the co-codamol for now and not take any more until he has spoken to a doctor or pharmacist. Check that he isn't taking other products containing paracetamol, such as cold and flu remedies, so he doesn't double up.

Call 999 or go to emergency care immediately if he develops any of the following: swelling of the lips, tongue, face or throat; difficulty breathing, wheezing or a tight chest; a rapid heartbeat or feeling like he may pass out; widespread hives spreading quickly; blistering or peeling skin, or sores in the mouth or eyes; or a high fever. The faintness he had yesterday is worth mentioning to a doctor, even though it has passed.

If none of those are present and he is otherwise well, he should still contact his GP, the surgery's urgent line, or NHS 111 (if you're in the UK) today, tell them about the rash and the timing relative to the tablets, and ask about an alternative painkiller. A pharmacist can also advise quickly and without an appointment.

For comfort in the meantime, he can take a non-drowsy antihistamine such as cetirizine or loratadine, which the pharmacist can confirm is safe alongside his other medicines. Keeping the skin cool, wearing loose cotton clothing, using lukewarm rather than hot showers, and applying a fragrance-free moisturiser or calamine lotion can ease itching. Try to avoid scratching, and avoid new soaps or lotions so you can tell what is causing the rash.

It may be worth noting when the rash appeared, whether it is spreading, and whether he has had any other new foods, medicines or exposures recently, as this helps the doctor work out the cause. If the rash is spreading or he feels worse at any point, seek urgent help rather than waiting.

Oklahoma is best known as a major energy producer. It ranks among the top states in the nation for crude oil and natural gas production, and the industry has shaped the state's economy and identity since the early 1900s. Cushing, Oklahoma, is a key oil storage and pipeline hub, and its prices serve as the benchmark for West Texas Intermediate crude. In recent years the state has also become one of the leading producers of wind energy, with large wind farms spread across its western plains.

Agriculture is another cornerstone of the economy. Cattle ranching is the state's most valuable agricultural sector, and Oklahoma is among the top beef cattle states in the country. Winter wheat is the leading crop, grown widely across the western and northern parts of the state. Farmers also produce hay, soybeans, corn, sorghum, cotton, canola, and peanuts, and the state has significant hog and poultry operations, particularly broiler chickens in the eastern region. Pecans are another notable crop, as Oklahoma is one of the larger pecan-producing states.

Beyond energy and farming, Oklahoma has a substantial aerospace and aviation industry, centered largely around Tulsa and Oklahoma City, including aircraft maintenance, repair, and manufacturing as well as Tinker Air Force Base. The state also manufactures machinery, fabricated metal products, rubber and plastic goods such as tires, and food products. Mining contributes resources like gypsum, limestone, sand, gravel, and iodine, and Oklahoma is notably the only U.S. state that produces iodine from underground brine deposits.

Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is a type of AI that can understand or learn pretty much any intellectual task a human can. You'll also see it called "strong AI" or "human-level AI." It's different from narrow AI, which is built for one job or a handful of jobs, like beating you at chess or picking faces out of a photo. AGI is meant to handle all of that and more: solving problems, picking up new concepts, understanding and using language, and adjusting to unfamiliar situations. It's a huge goal in the field and still gets a lot of research and arguing. Some people think it's doable and maybe not far off, while others aren't convinced. Either way, if it does happen, it'll probably change a lot of things about how we live.

Lots of people write about themselves in the third person on LinkedIn or a personal website because it can sound more polished and confident, like a professional bio you'd read in a conference program or a magazine article. Instead of saying "I lead a team of engineers," they write "Jane leads a team of engineers," which makes the text feel like someone else is describing their work. That can make big accomplishments sound more like facts and less like bragging, and it's easier to copy and paste into event programs, press kits, or guest speaker introductions without rewriting it.

Some people do it because they were told it's the standard for bios, and others find it easier to write about themselves that way because it creates a bit of distance, which can feel less awkward than saying "I'm great at this."

Your first-person approach is also perfectly good. Many readers find it warm and direct, and it makes it feel like you're talking to them personally, which is often what a portfolio or networking profile is for. The best choice mostly depends on your comfort and the tone you want. If you want something more formal, you could try third person in a short bio section, and keep first person elsewhere, like in your summary or project write-ups.

"A" and "R" reps are terms used in the mobile and telecom world, and in several other industries, to describe types of sales or service representatives, depending on context. The most common meaning comes from the wireless retail industry in the United States, where A reps and R reps refer to employees with different levels of performance or classification, often tied to commission structures. An A rep is typically a top-performing or high-volume salesperson who consistently meets or exceeds sales targets, while an R rep is usually a representative who is still developing or is in a more limited role, though the exact definitions vary by company.

The terms can also appear in other settings. In some call centers and customer support operations, letter grades like A and R may indicate a rep's skill level or the type of work they handle, such as account retention versus general inquiries. In certain industries, "R rep" can also refer to a representative handling returns or refunds.

If you saw these terms in a specific context, such as a job posting, a store, or a particular company, let me know and I can give you a more precise explanation.

Hot water freezing faster than cold water sounds backwards, but it's a real thing called the Mpemba effect. People usually assume the cold stuff should win the race, since it's already closer to freezing. The hot water's molecules are zipping around with more energy, which you'd think would make them harder to line up into the neat crystal pattern ice needs. So what's going on? Nobody has pinned it down yet. It got its name from Erasto Mpemba, a student who noticed it in the 1960s while making ice cream. Some researchers point to how heat escapes from the water into the air, others think dissolved impurities or evaporation play a role. It's also not something you can count on. Plenty of attempts show no effect at all, and it seems to depend on things like how pure the water is and how big the starting temperature gap is. So if you try it at home, don't be shocked if your cold tray loses.

Several common and treatable problems can cause this combination of symptoms. Pain that worsens when he sits up may point to pressure or bloating from gas, constipation, or a bowel blockage, or to gallbladder or pancreas trouble, which often causes belly pain after meals. Shakiness, weakness, and dizziness together, especially lasting weeks, often suggest the body isn't getting enough fluid, salt, sugar, or blood. Possible reasons include low blood sugar or uncontrolled diabetes, dehydration from poor eating or drinking, anemia from slow bleeding in the stomach or intestines (sometimes from an ulcer or from blood thinners or painkillers like ibuprofen), and an overactive thyroid, which can cause tremor and weight loss. Heart rhythm problems or low blood pressure can also cause dizziness and weakness, and medication side effects are a frequent cause in older adults. Less common but serious causes include a leaking or enlarging blood vessel in the belly, infection, and problems with the liver, kidneys, or adrenal glands.

Because the symptoms have lasted four weeks and he is getting weaker, he should be checked soon, even if he feels it may be nothing. A basic exam with blood tests (blood count, blood sugar, electrolytes, thyroid, and kidney and liver function) can identify many of these causes quickly and inexpensively. If cost is the barrier, an urgent care clinic, a telehealth visit, or a call to a local nurse advice line can be cheaper starting points, and a pharmacist can review his medications for side effects.

He needs emergency care right away, without waiting, if he faints or nearly faints, has severe or sudden worsening belly pain, a hard or swollen belly, vomits blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, has black or bloody stools, has chest pain, shortness of breath, confusion, trouble speaking, a fever with belly pain, or is too weak to stand or walk safely.

If it helps with the conversation, you might tell him that you are not asking him to assume the worst, only to rule out the treatable causes, and that a quick check now is usually far less costly than a delayed diagnosis later.

Abraham-Louis Breguet invented the tourbillon, and he was a Swiss watchmaker who worked in the late 1700s and early 1800s. He came up with it to make pocket watches more accurate, since gravity messes with the balance wheel depending on how the watch is positioned. The setup is basically a balance wheel and escapement mounted on a rotating cage that turns at a set rate, so the errors from each position get averaged out. Breguet patented it in 1801. Today it's a prized feature in high-end watches, and people still love it for the sheer craftsmanship.

Long ago, in the 1600s, a group of English people sailed across the ocean to build a new home in America. They were Puritans, which means they belonged to a strict kind of Christianity. They believed God was watching everything they did, and that the devil was always trying to trick people into doing bad things. They wanted their colony, Massachusetts Bay, to be a perfect village of believers, so they took church and rules very seriously.

Their lives were hard. Winters were cold, crops sometimes failed, and many families lost children to sickness. People often believed that when bad things happened, somebody must have caused them, and that the devil might be working through a person on Earth. This made them afraid, and fear can make people look for someone to blame.

The colony also had fights with its neighbors. Native American tribes and settlers clashed over land, and there were wars that scared everyone. Some colonists worried that enemies, or the devil, were hiding among them. The colony's government and church were closely tied together, so arguments about who was a good Christian could also become arguments about who was loyal to the community.

Trouble grew inside the town of Salem Village, which was part of the larger community. People there argued about money, land, and who should be their minister. Families split into groups that disliked each other, and these fights made people suspicious of their neighbors.

Then, in the winter of 1692, a few young girls in Salem Village started acting strangely. They had fits, screamed, and twisted their bodies. Doctors could not find a sickness, so the adults decided the girls must be bewitched. The girls named some women they said were witches. Once the first names were spoken, more and more people were accused. Many were poor, old, or different from their neighbors, and some were people the community already disliked.

Judges set up a special court to hear the cases. The rules let people be convicted based on things like claims that a spirit in the shape of the accused had hurt someone, which was hard to prove or disprove. Over the next several months, around 200 people were accused, about 30 were found guilty, and 19 were hanged. One man was pressed to death with heavy stones because he would not answer the charges. Eventually, people began to doubt the accusations, and the court was shut down. Later, the community felt deep regret, and years afterward some of the convicted were officially cleared.

So the Salem trials grew out of a frightened, strict religious community, hard living conditions, conflicts with neighbors, bitter local disputes, and a belief in the devil, all coming together when a few girls started a panic that spread out of control.

A faint line in the test window, next to a deep purple control line, is usually a positive result. The control line (the other window) only confirms the test worked, so its strength doesn't tell you how much pregnancy hormone is present. Any visible line in the test window, however faint, is generally read as pregnant under most manufacturers' instructions. The exception is an evaporation line, which is usually colourless or grey and appears after the reading time limit has passed. If your line was clearly visible within the time stated in the leaflet, it's more likely a real positive than an evaporation line.

Since you've had unprotected sex and your period is late, it's sensible to treat this as a probable pregnancy. Some caution is still worthwhile. Coming off the pill can delay your cycle for weeks, so a late period doesn't confirm anything on its own. Very early pregnancy can also produce faint lines that get darker over a few days. To check, use a fresh test with your first morning urine in two or three days, when hCG levels are usually higher, and read it within the time stated in the instructions. You can also book a blood test or appointment with your GP, a sexual health clinic, or a pharmacist, who can confirm the result and talk you through your options.

If you're pregnant and want to avoid it, act quickly, since some options work best within a limited time after sex. If you're unsure whether you're pregnant, you can get emergency contraception from a pharmacy or GP as soon as possible.

Whatever you decide, seek urgent medical help if you develop severe pain on one side of the abdomen, heavy bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, or dizziness or fainting, as these can signal an ectopic pregnancy.

So feral children are kids who grew up with basically no human contact or socialization, which means they never picked up language. Like, at all, in a lot of cases. Deaf people are a totally different situation. They've got language, usually sign language, or other ways of getting their point across, so they're not missing anything there.

People who don't have language still find ways to communicate. Gestures, facial expressions, body language, that kind of thing. Some use drawings or other visual stuff to say what they need or want. And some deaf folks or people with language impairments use tech to help out, like computers with speech synthesis, or they work with sign language interpreters.

Language isn't the only way to communicate, really. Someone who communicates differently, or doesn't have language, can express themselves and understand other people just as well as anyone else.

A semicolon is a punctuation mark that connects two sentences that are closely related in meaning. Think of it as a gentle bridge between two thoughts that belong together, but that are each complete enough to stand on their own. A period would stop the story completely, and a comma would make the bridge too weak, so the semicolon sits in the middle as a sturdy, friendly link.

Here is a simple example. "It was raining; we stayed inside." Both parts are complete sentences, and they are connected because the rain is the reason we stayed inside. You could also write "It was raining. We stayed inside." That works too, but the semicolon shows the two ideas are linked.

The semicolon has a second job, which is helping organize a list when the items themselves already contain commas. For instance, "We visited Paris, France; Rome, Italy; and Madrid, Spain." Without the semicolons, the reader would get confused about where one place ends and the next begins.

A helpful way to remember the first rule is this: if you could replace the semicolon with a period and both sides would still be full sentences, then a semicolon is an option. Just remember that it should never be used to introduce a list or to join a sentence to a fragment. If you are ever unsure, a period is almost always safe, and many good writers use semicolons only occasionally.

Charles Dickens was an English writer who lived from 1812 to 1870. He was born on February 7, 1812, in Portsmouth, England, and he died on June 9, 1870, in Kent. He got hugely popular in his own day, and people still love him now for his gripping storytelling, his unforgettable characters, and the way he took aim at the social problems of his time. If you've read any of his stuff, you've probably run into "Oliver Twist," "A Christmas Carol," "David Copperfield," or "Great Expectations."

It depends mainly on the contract terms and the reason the loan was denied, but the general rule is that the buyer gets the deposit back if the failure is covered by a contingency in the purchase agreement.

Most residential contracts include a financing contingency, which lets the buyer cancel the deal if they cannot obtain a mortgage on the agreed terms within a set period. If underwriting rejects the loan and the buyer cancels within that window, the earnest money is typically refunded in full. The buyer usually needs to deliver written notice of the cancellation before the contingency deadline, and the title or escrow company then releases the funds, often with both parties signing a mutual release.

Problems arise in a few situations. If the contingency period has already expired, the buyer may have waived the right to cancel without losing the deposit, and forfeiture becomes a real risk. If the buyer simply fails to qualify because of a change in their finances, such as a new debt or job loss, or fails to provide requested documents on time, the seller may argue the buyer breached the contract, and the seller could claim the deposit as liquidated damages. Disputes like this are often settled by negotiation, or by mediation or arbitration if the contract requires it, and sometimes a court decides who keeps the money.

Practically, buyers should read the contingency deadlines carefully, keep the lender informed, respond quickly to underwriting conditions, and consult their real estate agent or attorney before letting any deadline pass. Since rules vary by state and by the specific contract, anyone facing this situation should check the actual purchase agreement and local law.

The British Empire was basically a bunch of countries and territories run by the British government, and it covered a huge chunk of the world. Over time, though, people in many of those places started wanting real control over their own lives and governments. Lots of them pushed hard for independence, sometimes through outright fighting. That whole process of breaking away is called decolonization. As more countries split off, the empire shrank until it more or less fell apart.

Thank you for being open about this. Many men in their late twenties and thirties face low desire or erection problems, and they are very treatable. Please don't start or continue any tablet on your own, though, and especially not one taken every day.

Manforce contains sildenafil, which is a medicine for erection difficulty. It does not raise sex drive or change the size of the penis. It works only when you are sexually stimulated, and it is usually taken about 30 to 60 minutes before sex, no more than once in 24 hours. Taking 50 mg every day is not the usual way it is prescribed, and it can cause headache, flushing, dizziness, stuffy nose, stomach upset, and a drop in blood pressure. It is dangerous in combination with nitrate heart medicines and can interact with some other drugs. Because you are already taking tablets for your nerves or mood, you need your prescribing doctor to check that they are safe together.

The "psychology tablets" you mention are important here. Several common medicines for anxiety and depression, particularly the SSRI group, are well known to reduce libido and cause erection or ejaculation problems. Stress, anxiety about performance, and low mood can cause the same symptoms by themselves. So the cause of your low desire may be the medicine, the mental health condition, or both. Stopping an antidepressant suddenly can make you quite unwell, so do not stop it without medical advice. Instead, tell the doctor who prescribed it exactly what you are experiencing. They may adjust the dose, change the medicine, or add a treatment that suits you.

It would also help to see a doctor or urologist who can check your blood sugar, testosterone, thyroid function, and blood pressure, since these can all affect sexual function. Counselling or sex therapy is also very effective when anxiety about performance or the wedding is part of the picture, and many couples benefit from talking through these worries together.

As for after your marriage, there is no need to decide now that you will take Manforce for the rest of your life. Whether you need any medicine, and which one, depends on what the examination finds. Many men with this problem improve with treatment of the underlying cause, better sleep, regular exercise, less alcohol and smoking, and open communication with their partner.

Please see a doctor soon, before your wedding if possible, and bring a list of all the tablets you are taking.

Some folks write about themselves in the third person on LinkedIn or their personal websites because it comes across as more professional or formal. Instead of "I have a degree in computer science," they'd write "John has a degree in computer science." It makes the person sound a little more distant and objective, less like they're bragging. Others do it just to avoid saying "I" over and over, since that can start to feel self-centered. Honestly, it's mostly a matter of taste. Some people like first person because it feels more genuine, and others go third person because it sounds polished. Pick whatever fits you and your brand best.

A child with asthma and autism who suddenly turns pale may be showing signs of several different problems, such as anemia, low oxygen levels in the blood, or a heart condition. The paleness might also point to a breathing problem like an asthma attack, or it could be a medication side effect. Because it may indicate a serious health concern, you should get medical help if you see your child become pale all of a sudden. The child's doctor can evaluate the symptoms, identify what is causing the paleness, and recommend suitable treatment.

Yes, there really is a way, and it works for lots of people! Let me explain it like a story.

Imagine your brain has a little guard dog living inside it. This guard dog's job is to bark loudly whenever it thinks something dangerous is nearby, so you can stay safe. That's a good job! But sometimes the guard dog gets mixed up. It sees a tiny bug and thinks, "Oh no, a monster!" and starts barking like crazy. That barking is what makes your heart jump, your tummy feel funny, and your body want to run away. The bug isn't actually a monster, but your guard dog doesn't know that yet.

The trick to getting over a phobia is to teach your guard dog that bugs are okay. And the way you teach it is by letting it see bugs a little bit at a time, in a safe way, until it gets bored and stops barking. Grown-up doctors call this "exposure," which is a fancy word for "getting used to something slowly."

It works like climbing stairs, one small step at a time. First, you might just draw a picture of a bug or say the word "bug" out loud. When that feels easy, you might look at a cartoon bug. Then a real photo of a bug. Then a video of a bug crawling. Later, maybe you look at a real bug inside a closed jar from across the room. Then a little closer. You only move to the next step when the step you're on doesn't feel so scary anymore. Each time you stay with the scary feeling instead of running away, your guard dog learns, "Hey, nothing bad happened. Maybe I don't need to bark so much." Over time, the barking gets quieter and quieter.

While you practice, it helps to breathe slowly, like you're smelling a flower and then blowing out a birthday candle. Slow breathing tells your body, "We're okay, we're safe," and it helps calm that jumpy heart. It can also help to learn a few fun facts about bugs, because the more you understand them, the less mysterious and scary they seem. Most bugs are tiny, busy, and much more interested in their own little lives than in you.

If your fear feels really big, like it stops you from going outside or makes you feel panicky a lot, there are special helpers called therapists who are very good at this. They can walk with you up those stairs, one step at a time, so you never have to do it alone. Many people who were super scared of bugs end up feeling calm around them after some practice.

So the big idea is this: you don't get rid of the fear by hiding from bugs. You get rid of it by gently, slowly showing your brain that bugs aren't monsters. Your guard dog can learn, and so can you!

Okay so rechargeable batteries are built differently from regular ones so they can be used again and again. Regular batteries have chemicals inside that get used up when you run them, and once they're gone the battery is dead. Rechargeable ones use chemicals that can be used up and then restored by pushing electricity back in. Think of it like a glass of water you can empty and refill. Regular batteries just don't have the right kind of chemicals to be refilled like that.

In video games, "meta" just means the strategies everyone's actually using in competitive play. Those strategies pop up and change over time as players figure out what works best. Sometimes developers nudge things along on purpose, tweaking characters so certain combos are stronger than others. But a lot of the meta grows on its own, as people try stuff out and swap notes. You see this in pretty much any competitive game, whether it's a fighter like Street Fighter or a team shooter like Overwatch. Honestly, the players are the ones really shaping it. They're always testing new ideas and hunting for an edge, so the meta can shift fast. When that happens, devs sometimes have to step in with patches to keep things fair.

Belief revision refers to the way we adjust what we hold to be true when confronted with fresh evidence or information. It is a vital component of learning and of adapting to unfamiliar circumstances, and it allows us to build richer and more precise pictures of the world. This process can take several shapes. Sometimes it merely means incorporating a new belief into the collection we already hold; at other times it requires altering or discarding existing beliefs because of new evidence. It may also mean reconsidering what our existing beliefs signify or how they should be understood in light of new information. Scholars and practitioners approach belief revision in varied ways, ranging from formal methods that apply logic and mathematics to update beliefs, to more casual methods that depend on intuition and common sense. Whichever method is chosen, belief revision is central to our ongoing effort to refine and update our understanding of the world.

"Trust, but verify" basically means you can trust someone, but you should still double-check that what they're saying or doing is actually right. Say a friend tells you they'll meet you at the park at 3. You trust them to show up, but it's still smart to glance at your watch or phone so you're both on the same schedule. Checking the time doesn't mean you think your friend is lying or unreliable. You're just making sure you're on the same page. So trusting someone and verifying things can actually go hand in hand.

An adult human has 206 bones in total. This count can differ a little between individuals, since some people have additional bones, such as extra ribs, while others lack certain ones, like cervical ribs. The skeleton is split into two principal groups: the axial and the appendicular skeleton. The axial group contains 80 bones, covering the skull, the spinal column, and the rib cage. The appendicular group contains 126 bones, made up of the arms and legs, along with the shoulder girdle and the pelvis.

Several conditions, such as gout and arthritis, can lead to foot pain. The right approach depends on what is causing the pain, and it often combines self-care with medical care. Self-care options include giving your feet a rest by limiting time spent standing or walking and pausing regularly when you do need to be on them. Applying ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, several times daily, can ease swelling and inflammation. Over-the-counter drugs such as ibuprofen or naproxen, which belong to the nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory class, can also reduce pain and swelling. Gentle foot stretches may relieve discomfort and increase flexibility, and supportive, cushioned shoe inserts can make a difference as well. On the medical side, a doctor may prescribe stronger pain relievers or anti-inflammatory medication if over-the-counter options fall short. A physical therapist can show you exercises and stretches that reduce pain and improve movement. Corticosteroid injections can calm inflammation and discomfort in the foot. In serious cases, surgery may be needed to fix a structural problem causing the pain. Because the right treatment depends on an accurate diagnosis, it is important to see a healthcare professional about your foot pain.

Solving a Rubik's Cube in under 10 seconds is possible because fast cubers don't really solve it in one go. They learn a set of patterns, like memorized dance moves, that fix small groups of pieces at a time. Most of them use a method called CFOP, which stands for Cross, First two layers, Orientation, and Permutation. First they make a plus-shaped cross on one side. Then they tuck in the corner and edge pieces for the first two layers, usually one little pair at a time. Last, they flip and shuffle the top layer so every piece lands in the right spot.

The secret to speed is that they don't stop to think between moves. They look at the next step while their fingers are already doing the current one, so the cube keeps moving smoothly. They also use a trick called lookahead, where they spot the next piece they need while still finishing the one in front of them. Years of practice make the patterns feel automatic, almost like typing words instead of spelling out each letter.

Think of it like learning to tie your shoes. The first time, it takes forever. After thousands of tries, your hands just know what to do, and you can do it super fast without thinking hard about each loop.

So if you didn't get a paycheck you were expecting, you might be able to deduct the unpaid wages on your taxes, but it really depends on your situation. If you're an employee and you did the work but never got paid, you could possibly claim it as a miscellaneous itemized deduction. There are a few conditions, though. The wages have to be for work you actually did. You need to have properly reported them to your employer. They can't be for work from a previous year. And you need to have gotten a W-2 from your employer for the year you did the work, even if the paycheck never showed up.

If you check all those boxes, you'd take the deduction as an itemized deduction on Schedule A of Form 1040. One catch is that it's subject to a 2% of adjusted gross income (AGI) limit, so you can only deduct the part that goes over 2% of your AGI.

If you're self-employed and never got paid for work you did, it works differently. You might be able to deduct the unpaid amount as a business expense on Schedule C of Form 1040.

Honestly, with something like this I'd talk to a tax pro or look at the IRS guidelines before filing. They can tell you whether you actually qualify and help you get it done right.

Children naturally grow at varying speeds, and it is common for them to experience stretches of quicker or slower growth. Genetics has a major influence on how tall a child becomes, so your daughter may well be growing within the typical range for what her genes allow. Trying to boost a child's height with medical treatments or supplements is not recommended, since it can harm their general health and development. Kids are best served by growing at their own pace, with a focus on nutritious food and a healthy lifestyle that supports them. If you are worried about your child's growth, consulting a healthcare provider is the right step. They can evaluate her growth and development and offer advice on how to care for her health and well-being.

The dot com bubble refers to a stretch of late 1990s and early 2000s speculation and excitement around internet companies, especially those focused on online commerce. Over this period, the valuations of many such firms rose sharply, producing a bubble in the stock market. That bubble eventually popped, and share prices fell dramatically. Several causes contributed: internet firms had become overvalued, the growth in internet adoption slowed, and venture capital funding dried up. As their values dropped, numerous internet companies collapsed or ran into serious financial trouble, which in turn triggered mass job cuts and a broader contraction in economic activity. The bursting of the bubble had far-reaching effects on the world economy and helped bring on the recession of the early 2000s.

A wingman is a friend who assists you in meeting and mingling with new people, particularly when you're hoping to find a romantic connection. The wingman can break the ice by introducing you, getting conversations going, and offering general support and encouragement. Their purpose is to help you feel relaxed and self-assured rather than uncomfortable. For instance, a wingman might introduce you to a woman you like and then chat with her friend, leaving you free to talk with the woman who caught your eye. They may also say good things about you or your interests to the person you want to impress, or nudge the conversation toward topics that show you in a favorable light. It's worth remembering that a wingman should support you, not take control of the conversation or overshadow you. The real aim is for you to form a connection with the woman yourself, rather than having your wingman do the work for you.

I'm sorry you've been feeling this way, and I believe you that your body hasn't felt right since October. Your symptoms together need a real medical evaluation, and I'd recommend getting one today rather than waiting.

A temperature of 96.5 with chills, night sweats, abdominal tenderness, body aches, and fatigue can be a sign that your body is fighting an infection, and a low reading can sometimes happen when the body is under serious stress. Given your earlier IUD infection, the tenderness in your abdomen is worth taking seriously, because infections in the pelvic area can spread or form pockets of pus if they aren't fully treated. The rash on your arms and the cuts that won't heal well also need to be looked at, since they can be related to infection or to other conditions that a doctor can test for.

Please go to an emergency department or urgent care today if you notice any of these: confusion or unusual drowsiness, a racing or pounding heartbeat, dizziness or fainting, trouble breathing, a severe or rapidly worsening belly pain, heavy bleeding or foul-smelling discharge, a rash that spreads quickly or develops purple or dark spots, or a feeling that you're getting much sicker. These can be signs of a serious infection that needs fast treatment.

When you're seen, tell the provider clearly about the IUD infection in October, whether the device was removed, and every symptom you've listed, including the timing of the night sweats and the arm rash. Ask directly for blood tests such as a complete blood count and infection markers, a pregnancy test, and screening for sexually transmitted infections, and ask whether a pelvic ultrasound is needed to check for any leftover infection or problem related to the device. If you feel you're not being taken seriously, you can ask to speak with a doctor directly or to see a gynecologist, and it's reasonable to say, "I know my body has not been right since my infection, and I need someone to investigate."

In the meantime, rest, drink plenty of fluids, and keep yourself warm. Over-the-counter acetaminophen can ease the aches and headache, but check with a pharmacist first about the right dose for you, and avoid anything that might hide a fever before you've been examined. Please don't wait for these symptoms to pass on their own.

Technical analysis evaluates securities by studying statistics produced by trading activity, such as historical prices and volume. Analysts rely on charts and other tools to spot patterns that might signal when to buy or sell. Many indicators exist to support trading decisions, but several widely used ones are regarded as leading indicators, including the following. Moving averages smooth out price movements by averaging prices over a set period, such as the past 50 days. They help reveal trends and can produce buy and sell signals. The relative strength index (RSI) gauges the size of recent price changes to judge whether a security is overbought or oversold. A reading above 70 may indicate overbought conditions, while a reading below 30 may indicate oversold conditions. Moving average convergence divergence (MACD) compares two moving averages to detect shifts in trend and can also generate buy and sell signals. Bollinger Bands are bands drawn around a moving average that reflect how volatile a security is. When prices break outside these bands, a trend may be changing. Technical indicators should not be relied on alone, and most experts recommend combining several of them when making trading decisions. Finally, past performance does not guarantee future results, and technical analysis is only one of many ways to evaluate securities.

Batteries are built from a blend of materials that enable them to hold and discharge electrical energy. Which substances are chosen depends on the battery's category and what it is meant to do. Nearly every battery has at least two electrodes, a separator, and an electrolyte. Electrodes are usually metals like lead, nickel, or lithium, and a separator, typically a permeable material that lets ions travel across it, keeps them apart. The electrolyte, which may be a liquid or a gel, carries ions so they can shuttle between the electrodes. One electrode in a standard battery serves as the anode, while the other serves as the cathode. During operation, ions moving from the electrolyte pass through the separator and interact with the electrodes, triggering chemical reactions that either release or absorb electrical energy. Batteries fall into several groups. Primary batteries are single-use and thrown away after they run down, whereas secondary batteries can be recharged and reused many times. Although each kind has its own mix of materials and construction, all of them operate on the same fundamental principles for storing and delivering electricity.

Exchange-traded products (ETPs), such as exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and exchange-traded notes (ETNs), are investments that trade on a stock exchange in the same way as individual shares. Like every investment vehicle, ETPs levy charges to pay for their running costs, which include managing the portfolio, marketing, and administrative work. An investor who buys or sells an ETP may also owe a commission to the broker or financial firm that processes the trade. The size of this commission depends on the broker and the particular ETP, and it is usually deducted directly from the investor's account when the transaction takes place. Beyond these transaction charges, ETPs impose a recurring fee known as the expense ratio, which covers their operating costs. This ratio is a percentage of the ETP's assets, subtracted every year. To illustrate, an ETP with an expense ratio of 0.50% would cost an investor holding $10,000 of it $50 per year. The fees an ETP charges are generally built into its net asset value (NAV), meaning the worth of its underlying assets after liabilities are subtracted. Because the NAV drives the price at which the ETP trades on the exchange, the market factors these fees into the price. Higher fees can therefore push the price down, reflecting the greater cost to investors, while lower fees may allow the price to be higher, reflecting the reduced cost.

Generally, no. Premarket is usually harder for brokers to find shares to short, not easier. Securities lending, which is how brokers locate shares to borrow for short sales, runs on the regular market's infrastructure and inventory. Lending desks and the institutions that lend shares (pension funds, mutual funds, custodians) mostly operate during standard trading hours, so the pool of available borrow is thinner before the open. Borrow rates can also be higher or less predictable, and brokers may be more restrictive about accepting short orders in thinly traded or volatile names.

There are some nuances. Premarket trading itself is thinner, with lower volume and wider spreads, so executing a short there is costlier and riskier even if a share can be located. Some brokers do offer short selling in extended hours, but often only for a limited list of easy-to-borrow stocks, and they may apply their own restrictions. Locate requirements under Regulation SHO in the U.S. still apply, so a broker must have reasonable grounds to believe the shares can be borrowed before executing a short sale, regardless of the session.

If you're asking because you're considering a specific trade, check your broker's extended-hours short policy and the stock's borrow availability and fee, since those can vary a lot from day to day.
