Breathing often changes as well. It may become shallower, or it may turn into shorter, faster breaths. Some people also make unusual sounds while breathing, such as gurgling or wheezing. Nearer to the end, other bodily systems begin to fail: the heart rate can slow, blood pressure may fall, and the person may lose control of the bladder and bowels.

Keep in mind that everyone experiences dying differently, and not every person will go through all of these changes. Some die feeling peaceful and comfortable, while others experience pain or distress. It is also worth remembering that death is a natural part of life, and staying with a dying loved one can be a deeply meaningful and emotional experience.

Yellow teeth can come from a bunch of things. The big one is plaque, that sticky bacterial film that builds up on your teeth. If you don't get rid of it with brushing and flossing, it hardens into tartar, which is tough to scrub off and makes teeth look yellow. Other common culprits include drinking stuff that stains, like coffee, tea, or red wine, smoking or using tobacco, getting older (the enamel thins out and the dentin underneath shows through more), and certain medications that can discolor teeth.

As for brushing for an hour to get them super white? Sorry, that won't do it. Brushing and flossing help keep plaque and tartar in check, but they can't get rid of deeper staining the way whitening can. Professional whitening uses special products and procedures to lift stains and brighten things up, and you can get it done at a dentist's office or do it at home with a kit. If you're thinking about it, call a dentist first so they can tell you what'll work best for your teeth.

Whole brain emulation, sometimes called mind uploading or brain uploading, is a hypothetical procedure in which the information held in a biological brain is moved into a computer-based system or device. Its aim is either to produce artificial intelligence or to make a virtual duplicate of a person's consciousness. The idea rests on the assumption that the structure and workings of a brain can be fully understood and reproduced in a machine, and that the brain's computational processes can be simulated using software or hardware. The concept raises numerous technical and philosophical difficulties. One is how to faithfully capture and reproduce the intricate structure and function of a living brain. Others are the ethical and philosophical questions about what consciousness actually is and what might follow from creating artificial intelligence. Although certain researchers and futurists believe whole brain emulation may one day become achievable, it is still a highly speculative and contentious notion.

Not entirely. Freedom to provide services (Article 56 TFEU) stops Germany from discriminating against you because you are established elsewhere in the EU, but it does not exempt you from German taxes. Taxation remains a national competence, and the outcome depends on what you do, where you do it, and which double taxation treaty applies between your home country and Germany.

For income tax, the usual rule is that you are taxed where you are resident or established. Germany can still tax your profits if you have a permanent establishment there, such as a fixed place of business, a branch, or a construction site lasting beyond the period set by the treaty. Working for a German client from your home office generally does not create one, but a long on-site presence might.

For VAT, business-to-business services are generally taxed where the customer is established, so you usually invoice without German VAT and the German customer accounts for it under the reverse-charge mechanism. Services tied to immovable property, such as construction work on a site in Germany, are taxed where the property is located, so German VAT rules apply.

Germany also has specific withholding rules that can catch foreign providers. In the construction sector, the customer must generally withhold 15 percent of the payment for a foreign subcontractor unless you obtain an exemption certificate from the German tax office. Certain fees, such as those for artistic performances or some licensing, can also be subject to withholding under section 50a of the Income Tax Act. If you are an employee sent to Germany, social security rules may apply, and you would typically need an A1 certificate from your home country to stay under its system.

Because the details depend heavily on your activity, the length of your stay, and your treaty position, you should consult a tax adviser in both countries before starting work in Germany.

College is expensive for a few reasons. Colleges have lots of workers to pay, like teachers, researchers, advisors, and people who keep the buildings clean and safe. Many schools also build fancy things like gyms, dorms, and science labs, and those cost a lot of money to build and maintain. On top of that, students often get loans, and when lots of people can borrow money for school, colleges may feel they can charge more because the money is still there to pay for it.

Tuition has kept climbing for the last ten years for a few simple reasons. Schools have had less money from governments in many places, so they raise tuition to cover the gap. Health care costs for the people who work there have also gone up quite a bit. Schools have also competed with each other to attract students by offering nicer buildings and more activities, and those extras add to the bill. Some schools have also hired more administrators, the people who handle paperwork and rules, and their pay adds up too.

As for what could slow it down, there are a few ideas. If governments put more money into public colleges, schools would need to raise tuition less. If families and students become more careful about comparing prices and choosing schools that offer good value, colleges may have to keep their costs in check to compete. Some people also think that if schools find cheaper ways to teach, like online classes or shorter programs, prices could come down. Nobody knows for sure which of these will win out, but a mix of them would probably work best.

Post and lintel construction is one of the oldest and simplest structural systems in building. It consists of two basic elements: vertical supports called posts (or columns, piers, or jambs when they are part of a wall), and horizontal members called lintels (or beams, when they span larger distances) that rest across the tops of the posts. Together they form an opening or a framework that carries loads straight down through the verticals to the ground.

The system works by transferring weight. The lintel bears the load from above, such as a wall, roof, or floor, and passes it to the posts, which carry it into the foundation. Because the horizontal member is loaded in bending, its span is limited by the strength of the material. Stone, timber, and early concrete are all relatively weak in tension, so post and lintel designs generally work best with short spans. Ancient builders responded by placing posts closely together, which is why this method is seen in structures like Egyptian temples, Greek temples such as the Parthenon, and Stonehenge, where massive stone lintels were raised across upright stones.

Doorways and windows are the most common modern application. A lintel placed above an opening carries the wall material above it, so the wall does not press directly on the hole. Steel or concrete lintels are standard in brick and block construction, and wooden headers serve the same purpose in timber-framed houses.

The system also appears in larger framed structures. Steel and reinforced concrete frames are essentially post and beam systems, with columns supporting horizontal beams that carry floors and roofs. Modern buildings, from warehouses to office towers, rely on this principle, though with materials that allow much longer spans than ancient stone could achieve.

Post and lintel construction is valued for its simplicity, clarity of structure, and ease of construction, but it has limits. Large spans require either closely spaced supports or stronger, more expensive materials, and the system is less resistant to lateral forces such as wind or earthquakes unless it is braced. Despite these constraints, it remains a fundamental idea in architecture and engineering.

Think of the internet like a big playground, and the browser is the door you walk through to get in. Whoever builds the door gets to decide a lot about what you see first when you step inside.

When you use Edge, Microsoft gets to be the one who greets you. Edge opens to a page that Microsoft designs, with Bing as the default search, Microsoft news and shopping suggestions, and links to other Microsoft things. That ties directly to the ad money you already understand. Every search that happens in Edge instead of Chrome is a search that Bing gets by default, and most people never change the default. So pushing Edge is really part of pushing Bing. If people use Chrome, Google's search is the default door, and Google collects the money.

There is also a second reason, which is control. If one company, Google, owns the most popular browser, it can decide how the web works. It can make rules about what websites are allowed to do, how ads get tracked, and which new features exist. Microsoft does not want to depend on a rival for the way people reach its own services, like Office on the web, Outlook, Teams, and its AI assistant Copilot. Owning a browser means Microsoft can make those things work smoothly and show them off to you.

Third, a browser collects useful information about what people like and do online, which helps with advertising and with improving products. Users who sign into Edge with a Microsoft account also tend to stay inside Microsoft's world, using more of its apps and services, and that keeps them loyal.

Finally, there is history. Microsoft once had the most popular browser, Internet Explorer, and then lost it to Chrome. Windows is how most people get to a computer in the first place, so Microsoft feels it should be natural for its own browser to be the one you use. It is a bit like a toy store wanting to be the one to hand you the toys, instead of letting the shop next door do it.

So the short version: the browser is the front door to the internet, and whoever runs the door gets more search money, more control, more information, and more people staying in their own neighborhood.

Alcohol makes you sleepy at first, but it messes up your sleep in the second half of the night. Think of your body's sleep as a bedtime routine with lots of steps, and alcohol bumps the steps out of order. Your body also has a built-in clock that tells it when to wake up, and alcohol can make that clock go off too soon.

Drinking a lot also makes your body need to pee more, and it dries you out, which can wake you up. When the alcohol wears off in the middle of the night, your body gets a little jolt, like a tiny alarm, and that can wake you before you have had enough sleep.

So you feel knocked out at first, then you pop awake early and have trouble falling back asleep. Drinking more water and having a little less alcohol can help a lot.

So No Child Left Behind was a federal education law that George W. Bush signed on January 8, 2002. The idea was to lift the performance of public schools by holding them more accountable, giving states and districts more room to run things their own way, and letting parents pick better options for their kids. A big goal was closing the achievement gap between disadvantaged students and everyone else. States had to set measurable targets for student performance and step in when schools kept missing them. It got a lot of pushback, and it was eventually replaced by the Every Student Succeeds Act in 2015.

Basically we crank up the heat in winter because it's cold out, and when it's cold out our bodies feel it too. So we warm the house up to feel comfortable and cozy. Summer's the opposite. It's warmer outside, so there's no need to run the heat much, and a lot of people switch on the AC to stay cool instead.

Keeping the house at a comfortable temperature matters more than you'd think, since it can affect your health and how you feel day to day. If it's too cold inside, you can end up sick or just plain miserable. Too hot, and you're uncomfortable and probably not sleeping well either. Get the temperature right and you tend to feel good and stay healthier.

A disulfide bond is a covalent bond formed between the sulfur atoms of two cysteine residues in a protein. Each cysteine contributes a thiol group (-SH), and when two of these groups are brought close together and oxidized, they join through a shared sulfur-sulfur bond, with the loss of two hydrogen atoms. The result is a cystine unit, written as -S-S-, which links the two parts of the polypeptide chain together.

Structurally, the bond itself is a single S-S linkage, roughly 2.05 angstroms long, and the atoms around it tend to adopt a characteristic dihedral angle, usually near 90 degrees, which constrains how the chain can fold. Disulfide bonds can connect two cysteines within the same chain, creating a loop that stabilizes a local fold, or they can link separate chains together, as in insulin, where the A and B chains are held by disulfides. They are most common in proteins that are secreted or exposed to the extracellular environment, such as antibodies and many hormones, because the oxidizing conditions there favor their formation. Inside the reducing environment of the cell cytoplasm, they generally do not form, which is one reason intracellular proteins rely on other forces to maintain their shape.

Imagine you're telling a story about a very special baby. In the Christian story, that baby, Jesus, isn't just a regular person. Christians believe he is God's own son who came to live as a human. So the story says Jesus didn't have a regular human daddy. Instead, God made the baby grow inside Mary in a miraculous way. Mary being a virgin means she hadn't been with a man, so the only way she could be having a baby was through God. It's like a big sign that says, "This baby came from God, not just from people."

So it wasn't really something that "just happened." In the story, it's the whole point. The way Jesus was born shows who Christians think he is. He has a human mom, which makes him truly human, and God as his father, which makes him truly divine. Both parts matter in Christian belief.

There's another reason too. Long before Jesus, there was an old book of prophecies, and one line (in the book of Isaiah) talked about a young woman having a special baby. The writers of the Gospels of Matthew and Luke saw Jesus's birth as that old promise coming true, a bit like finding the missing puzzle piece that finally fits.

Later, some Christian thinkers added another idea. They believed humans pass a kind of "brokenness," called original sin, down from parent to child, and they saw the virgin birth as part of how Jesus could be born pure and without that brokenness. Not all Christians explain it this way, but it became an important idea for many.

Is it symbolism or a real event? That depends on who you ask. Many Christians believe it really happened exactly as described, as a true miracle. Some Christians see it mainly as a meaningful way of expressing who Jesus is. And historians who study religion often point out that ancient stories sometimes gave great figures special or miraculous births to show how important they were. So for believers it is both a real event and full of meaning, and for others it's a powerful symbol in a very old and important story.

Hi there! Scientific Creationism is a way some Christians understand how the world began. They believe the Bible is true, and that God made everything.

The Bible's first book, Genesis, says God made the whole world in six days. He made light, then the sky, then land and plants, then the sun, moon, and stars, then fish and birds, then animals and people. On the seventh day He rested. People who believe in Scientific Creationism take those words very seriously, as if each day were an ordinary day, about 24 hours long.

They also think God made each kind of animal and plant separately, so a dog stayed a dog and a cat stayed a cat, rather than one kind slowly turning into another over millions of years.

Many of them also believe a huge flood once covered the whole Earth in the time of Noah, and that the flood helped shape the rocks and mountains we see today.

Because they care about science, they look at rocks, fossils, and stars and try to explain what they find using their belief that God made the world only a few thousand years ago. Most scientists disagree. They say the rocks and stars show the Earth is billions of years old and that living things changed slowly over time. Many Christians agree with the scientists and believe God used those slow changes to make the world, so they don't read Genesis as a science book.

So Scientific Creationists trust the Bible's words about how long ago things happened, while most other scientists and many Christians read the same world in a different way. Christians can love each other and keep talking about these questions with kindness.

People may skip a personal liability umbrella insurance policy for several reasons. The first is price. These policies can be fairly costly, particularly for those with a high net worth or many assets to safeguard, and some individuals conclude that the extra protection isn't worth the premium. The second is a lack of need. If your activities don't expose you to a high risk of lawsuits, or if you don't own much that could be lost, an umbrella policy may seem unnecessary. The third is limited coverage. Umbrella policies often exclude certain claims, such as those arising from professional liability or business activities, so if those are your main worries, this type of policy may not suit you. The fourth is the presence of other coverage. Some people believe their home or auto insurance already gives them enough protection and therefore forgo an umbrella policy. In the end, choosing whether to buy one is a personal decision that rests on your own situation and level of risk.

"Wild Bill" most often refers to Wild Bill Hickok, the frontier lawman and gunfighter. I don't have reliable details about how his father, William Alonzo Hickok, died. I believe he lived until the early 1870s, but I can't confirm the date or cause, so I'd rather not guess. If you tell me which Wild Bill you mean, or where you came across the question, I can try to help further. A biography of Hickok or a historical source like the Kansas Historical Society would also have accurate details.

Getting an MRI after orthognathic surgery is usually safe, whatever kind of metal was used during the operation. Titanium is a popular choice for surgical implants, orthognathic procedures among them, and it is typically regarded as MRI-safe. Even so, you should tell both the MRI technologist and the radiologist about any earlier surgery in which metal implants or other foreign objects were placed. That detail goes on the MRI safety screening questionnaire and helps the medical team select the most suitable MRI protocol for you.

If you want to find out which metal was used in your earlier jaw surgery, you can contact the hospital or clinic that performed it and request a copy of your medical records. Those records should list the materials used, including the metal of the plates and screws. Alternatively, you can ask your surgeon or another provider who took part in your care for the information. If you cannot get it, or if you are worried about whether the MRI is safe, talk over your options with the MRI technologist, the radiologist, or your primary care provider. They can work out the best way forward given your particular circumstances.

Several personal finance applications can be used on Mac, iOS, and Windows. Among them are Mint, a free tool that helps you monitor expenses, set up a budget, and receive tailored suggestions for saving money, and Personal Capital, which provides budgeting, investment monitoring, and retirement planning in one package. Both are compatible with all three platforms. Acorns is another option, designed for investing with modest sums, and it also runs on all three. YNAB, short for You Need a Budget, focuses on giving you control over your funds so you can meet your financial goals, and it works on each of these systems as well. Quicken rounds out the list as a comprehensive money management program offering budgeting, bill tracking, and investment tracking, again available across all three platforms. Keep in mind that an app's features may vary depending on which platform you use it on. Comparing several options before deciding is a wise approach to finding the one that suits you best.

Futures studies, or futurology if you want the fancier name, is basically the practice of looking at where trends and events might be heading and trying to make sense of it. It's pretty interdisciplinary too. It pulls from economics, politics, sociology, psychology, anthropology, and science and tech, so it's not really stuck in one box.

The idea isn't to predict one exact future, though. It's more about laying out a range of possible futures, along with the risks and opportunities that come with each one. That helps people making decisions or setting policy, and it can help regular people and organizations get ready for changes and adapt when they hit.

The usual toolkit includes scenario planning, trend analysis, and modeling. With those you can pick out the main drivers of change, figure out how likely and how big different events might be, and weigh what would happen if you went with one policy or strategy over another.

The topic range is huge. Economic, social, technological, environmental, and political trends all fall under it. Some of the areas people dig into a lot are demographics, globalization, technological change, environmental sustainability, and global governance.

Imagine you have a collection of stickers that you get for free just by visiting a playground. Some kids want those stickers so badly that they will pay you a little bit of their allowance for them. You never had to work for them, but other kids think they look cool, or they want to finish a set, or they like trading them to show off. That is basically what Steam trading cards are.

Here is how it works in simple steps. When you play certain games on Steam, the game gives you little digital cards as a surprise, sometimes just for playing for a while. Each card is a picture, and some games have sets of cards that go together. If you collect a whole set, you can turn it into a small reward called a badge, and the badge shows off on your profile so people know you finished it. Some people love collecting badges the way kids love collecting stickers.

Steam also has a marketplace where people can buy and sell these cards with real money. The cards are worth very little, usually a few cents, but there are so many players and so many cards that the total adds up. Some people also buy cards to craft the badges faster, or to trade for other games' cards. Because lots of people want to finish sets, the price can go up a bit, and that is how you ended up with a dollar from items you got while having fun.

So the simple answer is this: people pay for the cards because they want the fun of collecting and finishing sets, and the marketplace lets you turn those extra surprises into a little bit of real money. It is not a lot, but it is a real trade, and you earned it by playing games you already enjoyed.

Visible light is the portion of the electromagnetic spectrum that the human eye can detect. Electromagnetic radiation travels as waves, and these waves vary in wavelength and frequency. Visible light occupies a narrow band, roughly between 380 and 750 nanometers in wavelength, though these limits vary slightly from person to person. Within this range, different wavelengths are perceived by our eyes as different colors. Longer wavelengths near 700 nanometers appear red, while shorter wavelengths near 400 nanometers appear violet. In between lie the familiar colors of the rainbow: orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo.

Sunlight is the most common natural source of visible light, and it contains all of these wavelengths mixed together, which is why it appears white. Artificial sources such as light bulbs, screens, and flames also emit visible light. Radiation just outside this range, such as ultraviolet and infrared, cannot be seen by people, although some animals, like bees, can perceive ultraviolet light.

The Matrix, the 1999 science fiction film, was written and directed by the Wachowskis, Lana and Lilly Wachowski. The sisters had previously made the crime thriller Bound in 1996, and The Matrix became their breakthrough work. The film was produced by Joel Silver and released by Warner Bros., with Village Roadshow Pictures as a co-financier.

The movie starred Keanu Reeves as Neo, Laurence Fishburne as Morpheus, Carrie-Anne Moss as Trinity, and Hugo Weaving as Agent Smith. Its famous action sequences were choreographed by martial arts legend Yuen Woo-ping, and its groundbreaking "bullet time" visual effects were supervised by John Gaeta, work that earned the film an Academy Award for Best Visual Effects among its four Oscar wins.

The Wachowskis went on to write and direct the sequels The Matrix Reloaded and The Matrix Revolutions, both released in 2003, and Lana Wachowski directed the fourth film, The Matrix Resurrections, in 2021.

A Master Limited Partnership is a business structure that combines features of a partnership with the trading convenience of a public company. It is organized as a limited partnership, but its ownership units trade on a major stock exchange like shares do. To qualify for partnership tax treatment, the law generally requires that at least 90 percent of its income come from qualifying sources, which are mostly natural resources and energy activities such as oil and gas pipelines, storage, processing, and coal, along with some real estate and commodity-related businesses. That is why most MLPs are found in the energy midstream sector.

The biggest difference from a plain stock is taxation. A regular corporation pays income tax on its profits, and then shareholders pay tax again on the dividends they receive. An MLP pays no entity-level federal income tax. Instead, income, deductions, and credits pass through to the unitholders, who report their share on their own tax returns. This avoids the double taxation that corporations face, which is one reason MLPs can pay generous distributions.

Other differences follow from the structure. Investors are called unitholders, not shareholders, and they are limited partners. The business is run by a general partner, who often holds incentive distribution rights that give it a growing share of cash flow as distributions rise. That can create conflicts of interest and lessen returns for ordinary unitholders. Limited partners generally have far weaker voting rights than corporate shareholders.

MLPs usually pay quarterly distributions rather than dividends, and the yields are often higher than those on typical stocks. Much of the distribution is often treated as return of capital, which is not taxed immediately but instead lowers your cost basis. This defers taxes, but when you sell, a portion of the gain may be taxed as ordinary income through depreciation recapture, and the lowered basis increases your taxable gain.

The paperwork is also different. Instead of a Form 1099, unitholders receive a Schedule K-1, which tends to arrive later and can be complicated, and may require filing in multiple states where the MLP operates. Holding MLPs in an IRA or other tax-deferred account can create unrelated business taxable income, so they are often a poor fit there. Many mutual funds and ETFs avoid these issues, though they bring their own tax and fee quirks.

Finally, risks include sensitivity to energy prices and volumes, heavy debt loads, and dependence on capital markets to fund growth, since the high payout leaves little retained cash. In short, an MLP offers tax-advantaged income and exchange liquidity, but with more tax complexity and governance trade-offs than ordinary stock.

Thinking about getting a down payment from a family member? There are tax angles to check first. If it's a gift, the giver might owe gift tax on it. For most people this isn't a problem, since the annual exclusion is $15,000 per recipient right now. But if the amount is bigger than that, the family member may have to pay gift tax or file a gift tax return.

If it's a loan instead, a few things matter. Get a written loan agreement that spells out the repayment schedule, the interest rate if there is one, and any other terms. Also think about your credit. A loan from family usually doesn't get reported to the credit bureaus, so it won't move your score either way. That's good or bad depending on where you stand. If your credit is already solid, it probably won't hurt you. If your credit is thin or shaky, it also won't help you build it.

Make the payments on time, even if Uncle Joe isn't charging interest. Sticking to the agreement builds a repayment history and keeps things friendly. And know that if you can't pay, the family member could take legal action, which can get messy fast and strain relationships for years.

Honestly, before you sign anything, it's worth talking to a financial advisor or a tax pro. They can look at your specific situation and catch things I've missed.

A stock dividend is called a dividend because it is a distribution of value to shareholders in proportion to their existing holdings, which is the defining feature of any dividend. In a cash dividend, the company pays shareholders money; in a stock dividend, it pays them additional shares of its own stock instead. Accounting rules reflect this. When a company declares a stock dividend, it typically moves an amount from retained earnings into common stock and additional paid-in capital, so the distribution is recorded as a transfer within shareholders' equity, much as a cash dividend reduces retained earnings. Shareholders who receive the new shares end up with a larger number of shares, and the company's directors have formally declared the distribution, which is why it carries the dividend label.

A stock split is different in both purpose and accounting. A split simply divides the existing shares into a larger number of shares, such as a two-for-one split that doubles the share count and halves the price per share. No earnings are transferred and no distribution is made; the only change is the number of units representing the same ownership. Companies usually split their stock to make the share price more affordable or more attractive to retail investors. Under accounting rules, a split generally only adjusts the par value and share count, while a stock dividend, particularly a small one, is recorded at market value and moves earnings into permanent capital.

The practical difference is that a stock dividend gives shareholders new shares as a distribution from the company's earnings, whereas a split changes how existing shares are divided without distributing anything. In both cases, each shareholder's proportional ownership of the company stays the same, so neither creates value by itself.

Before the United States acquired Alaska, it was controlled by the Russian Empire. Russian explorers, beginning with the expedition led by Vitus Bering in 1741, reached the region, and Russian fur traders soon followed, drawn by the valuable sea otter pelts. Russia established its first permanent settlement on Kodiak Island in 1784, and in 1799 the Russian-American Company was chartered to manage the colony and its fur trade, with its capital eventually based at New Archangel, now known as Sitka.

By the mid-1800s, Russia found the territory difficult to defend and costly to maintain, especially after the Crimean War strained its finances and raised fears that Britain might seize it from neighboring Canada. Russia therefore agreed to sell Alaska to the United States in 1867 for 7.2 million dollars, a deal negotiated by Secretary of State William Seward. Critics at the time mocked the purchase as "Seward's Folly," but it later proved highly valuable, especially after gold and oil were discovered.

Long before any European presence, Alaska was home to many Indigenous peoples, including the Iñupiat, Yup'ik, Aleut (Unangan), Tlingit, Haida, Athabascan, and others, who had lived there for thousands of years. Russian control was largely concentrated along the coasts and islands, and much of the interior remained under the practical control of these Native communities throughout the Russian period.

Multivariate statistics is the branch of stats that deals with multiple variables and how they relate to each other. Unlike univariate stats, which looks at just one variable at a time, multivariate methods let you look at several at once. You can use them for regression, classification, cluster analysis, and plenty more. They're big in psychology, economics, and marketing, since those fields usually juggle a bunch of variables at once. Some common techniques are principal component analysis, multivariate regression, and multivariate ANOVA. They help you untangle complicated relationships between variables and make predictions based on them. If you've got lots of variables to work with, it's a really handy toolkit.

Most organized baseball leagues play nine innings in an official game. Little League, though, usually plays six or seven, depending on the age group and the setup. In pro ball, if the score's still tied after nine, they just keep going into extra innings until someone wins. Really, it all comes down to whatever rules the league or tournament is using.

Generally speaking, retired couples benefit from spreading their investments across a range of assets, such as stocks, bonds, and cash. Doing so can reduce overall risk and may produce a consistent flow of income. Several specific approaches are worth considering.

First, set aside a "cash cushion" equal to at least six months of living costs. This reserve can cover unexpected bills or weather a market slump, offering peace of mind and making sure essential needs remain funded. Second, think about holding a blend of stocks and bonds. Stocks tend to offer greater returns over the long run but carry more risk, whereas bonds usually carry less risk and tend to yield lower returns. Holding both can help balance the danger of losses while still generating reliable income. Third, look at investments that pay out regularly, such as dividend-paying shares or bonds that make periodic interest payments. These can add a steady income stream that supports existing retirement savings. Finally, consider buying an annuity, a financial product that pays a guaranteed income either for a fixed term or for the remainder of your life. Annuities suit retirees who want a dependable income source, though they come with drawbacks and are not appropriate for everyone.

Ultimately, every couple's circumstances are different, and a strategy that suits one pair may not suit another. Partnering with a financial advisor to build a plan tailored to your particular needs and goals is a sensible step.

Coca-Cola and Pepsi are two well-known carbonated soft drinks that both emerged in the late 1800s. Each is made from carbonated water, sugar, flavorings, and caffeine. Still, the two companies use slightly different formulas, and people often favor one based on how it tastes. Part of Coca-Cola's popularity may come from its longer history: it was introduced in 1886, seven years before Pepsi appeared in 1893. That head start gave Coca-Cola more time to grow familiar and become a household name. Coca-Cola also benefits from a stronger brand identity. Its red and white colors and distinctive cursive logo have stayed clear and consistent over the years, helping it stand apart from other soft drinks and remain recognizable worldwide. In the end, whether someone prefers Coca-Cola or Pepsi comes down to personal taste, since some people simply enjoy one flavor more than the other.

It's understandable to wonder about this, and you're right that it's very early for typical pregnancy symptoms to be clear. Still, let me explain what's plausible so you can make sense of what you're feeling.

Pregnancy can't be detected by a test until roughly the time of a missed period, and symptoms like cramping or back ache can occur in the days before that, especially when an egg has just been fertilized and implantation is happening. Implantation cramping or spotting can start around 6 to 12 days after ovulation, so a few days of lower back and abdominal discomfort in your situation is possible with pregnancy. But these same symptoms are also very common with other things: the days leading up to a period, ovulation pain (mittelschmerz), constipation or bloating, gas, a urinary tract infection, or muscle strain from exercise or posture. Stress and changes in sleep or diet can also delay a period, so a late period on its own doesn't confirm anything.

Some practical steps may help. If your period is due and hasn't arrived, you can take a home pregnancy test. Testing with first-morning urine from about the day your period is expected, or a few days after if you want more reliability, gives the most accurate result. If the test is negative and your period still hasn't come after a week or so, test again or see a doctor, since a negative early test doesn't rule everything out. A blood test from a clinic or doctor can detect pregnancy a bit earlier than urine tests.

Please contact a doctor promptly, and don't wait, if you have severe or one-sided abdominal pain, heavy bleeding, dizziness or fainting, fever, pain when urinating, or pain that keeps getting worse. Those can signal a problem such as an ectopic pregnancy, which needs urgent care.

If you're trying to conceive, it's also worth knowing that a single missed period after a few weeks of trying is common and not necessarily a sign of a problem. If you test negative and periods stay irregular or you've been trying for several months without success, a doctor can help.

Microsoft created Bing, a web search engine that debuted in 2009 to take the place of Live Search, the engine Microsoft had relied on up to that point. Satya Nadella, today the chief executive of Microsoft, oversaw Bing's development, and the company built it to rival major competitors such as Google and Yahoo. Over the years Bing has kept growing and getting better, and it remains a widely used option for people searching for information online.

The phrase "HST compensation" can mean a few different things in Ontario, so it helps to sort out which situation you're in.

If you are an employee who paid HST on work-related expenses that your employer didn't reimburse, you can claim a rebate using Form GST370, the Employee and Partner GST/HST Rebate Application. This applies to employees who are required to pay their own expenses, such as vehicle costs, supplies, or home office expenses, and who have a signed Form T2200 from the employer confirming the conditions of employment. You file GST370 with your personal return, and the CRA calculates the rebate. You then also need to reduce the expenses you deduct on your income tax return by the GST/HST portion, since you can't claim the tax twice. The same form is available to partners of a partnership who paid expenses personally.

If you are self-employed and registered for GST/HST, you don't claim a rebate on your personal return. Instead you claim input tax credits on your GST/HST return, which you file separately, and which offsets the HST you collected. If you are self-employed but not registered, you generally can't recover HST paid, though it becomes part of your deductible business expense on form T2125.

If you're asking about the Ontario low-income benefit, there isn't an HST rebate in the old sense, but the federal GST/HST credit is a quarterly payment for low and modest income individuals and families. You don't need to claim it separately: you just file your tax return, even if you had no income, and the CRA assesses your eligibility automatically. Ontario also has a separate Ontario Trillium Benefit, which you apply for on your return by completing the Ontario Trillium Benefit section (Form ON-BEN), and it bundles energy and property tax credits and the sales tax credit.

If you tell me whether you are an employee, self-employed, or just looking for the low-income credit, I can walk you through the exact steps and lines on the return. In every case, keep your receipts, since the CRA may ask to see them.

A computer network consists of several computers linked together so they can share resources, swap files, and communicate. These machines may be joined by physical cables or by wireless signals, and they may sit side by side in one room or be spread across distant sites. Networks are grouped into categories according to their scale, the physical distance separating their machines, and the kinds of links that tie them together. A local area network (LAN), for instance, links computers within a confined space like an office or a house, whereas a wide area network (WAN) reaches across a broad region, such as multiple cities or entire nations. Networks can also be categorized by topology, meaning the arrangement of their connections. Common layouts include the star, in which every computer attaches to a central hub or switch; the bus, in which all computers share a single central cable; and the ring, in which each computer connects to two others in a circular loop. Today, networks play a vital role in computing, since they let machines share resources and talk to one another, which makes possible the flow of information and the construction of distributed systems.

I'm sorry you're dealing with this. Ongoing symptoms that haven't improved with treatment need a more thorough look, and you deserve clear answers rather than continuing medicines that aren't helping.

It's worth understanding what you've been prescribed. Motinorm-DT contains domperidone, which mainly helps with nausea, bloating, and slow stomach emptying. Nexito Plus contains escitalopram (an antidepressant) and clonazepam (a calming medicine), which doctors sometimes give when they suspect a functional gut problem such as irritable bowel syndrome, because stress and the gut-brain connection strongly affect digestion. Neither medicine treats liver disease or the cause of bleeding, so the lack of improvement suggests the underlying problem may not yet be fully identified. Please don't stop these tablets suddenly, especially the clonazepam, because that can cause withdrawal effects. Talk to your doctor about tapering or changing them.

I would strongly recommend seeing a gastroenterologist or hepatologist (liver specialist) if you haven't already. A normal colonoscopy is reassuring because it largely rules out colon cancer, polyps, and inflammatory bowel disease in the large intestine. But chronic diarrhea with blood still needs explanation, and with a liver problem there are other possibilities to check. Useful tests might include liver function tests, hepatitis B and C screening, an abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan to assess fatty liver or scarring, an upper endoscopy to look at the stomach and esophagus (which also helps evaluate acidity and, in liver disease, swollen veins), stool tests for infections such as amoebiasis or giardia, which are common causes of chronic dysentery, a celiac disease test, and a blood count to see whether the bleeding has caused anemia. It also helps to know exactly what "chronic liver problem" you've been diagnosed with, because fatty liver, hepatitis, alcohol-related disease, and others are managed very differently.

In the meantime, some everyday measures support both the liver and the gut. Avoid alcohol completely, since it worsens almost every liver condition and irritates the stomach. Eat smaller, regular meals, and cut down on fried, spicy, very oily, and processed foods. Avoid lying down for two to three hours after eating if you have acidity. Drink plenty of clean, safe water and use oral rehydration solution during diarrhea episodes. If you're overweight, gradual weight loss is one of the most effective treatments for fatty liver. Avoid painkillers like ibuprofen or diclofenac, which can cause stomach bleeding, and check with your doctor before taking herbal or "liver tonic" products, since some can actually harm the liver.

Seek urgent care if you notice large amounts of blood, black tarry stools, vomiting blood, yellowing of the eyes or skin, swelling of the abdomen or legs, confusion or excessive drowsiness, severe abdominal pain, fever, dizziness, or unexplained weight loss.

If you can share your actual liver test results, ultrasound findings, or the specific diagnosis your doctor gave, I can help you understand them and prepare questions for your next appointment.

Rule-based programming is a paradigm in which a program's behavior is expressed as a collection of rules, each typically written as a condition paired with an action, rather than as a sequence of step-by-step instructions. Each rule says, in effect, "if these conditions hold, then do this." The program works by checking which rules apply to the current set of facts or data and then executing the appropriate actions, often repeating this process until no further rules apply or a goal is reached.

A typical rule-based system has three main parts. The first is a knowledge base or working memory, which holds the facts the system knows about the world, such as sensor readings, customer attributes, or medical symptoms. The second is the rule base, a set of if-then statements that encode domain expertise. The third is an inference engine, a general-purpose component that matches the rules against the facts, selects which rules to fire, and carries out their actions. Because the inference engine is separate from the rules, developers can add, modify, or remove rules without rewriting the control logic of the whole program.

This approach is especially useful in domains where knowledge is easier to state declaratively than to encode in procedural code. Expert systems for medical diagnosis, tax or insurance eligibility checks, fraud detection, and business policy engines have historically relied on it. Many modern tools also use rules, such as complex event processing platforms, spam filters, and workflow engines. Popular languages and frameworks for this style include CLIPS, Drools for Java, and Prolog, which is closely related and uses logical rules to derive conclusions.

The main advantages are that rules are often easier for domain experts to read and verify, the system's reasoning can be traced by looking at which rules fired, and changing behavior is often a matter of editing rules rather than restructuring code. The drawbacks include the risk that large rule sets become hard to manage, with unexpected interactions between rules, and that performance can degrade as the number of rules and facts grows. Handling uncertainty, conflicting rules, and rule priority also requires careful design.

Daydreaming is often a natural and even beneficial part of mental life, yet when it starts getting in the way of concentration and getting things done, several approaches can help you regain control. Consider the following. First, pay attention to what tends to set off your daydreams and work to reduce or remove those factors where possible. For instance, if your mind wanders during a dull lecture, you might look for ways to make the material more interesting or take short breaks and switch to other activities. Second, establish clear objectives and deadlines. Well-defined goals can sharpen your focus and drive, making it harder for your thoughts to drift. Third, cultivate mindfulness by staying attentive to the here and now, which keeps you anchored and attentive. Practices like slow breathing or meditation can be woven into your everyday schedule. Fourth, when boredom or lack of interest leads you to drift off, pick an activity that fully captures your attention, such as a hobby, a puzzle, or a demanding task. Finally, if managing your daydreaming on your own proves too difficult, reach out for help from a mental health professional or someone you trust, such as a friend or relative. They can help uncover any underlying causes and work with you to build effective ways of handling it.

Pleural effusion, sometimes called lung effusion, occurs when fluid builds up in the narrow gap between the membranes that cover the lungs and the inner wall of the chest. As this fluid accumulates, it can compress the lungs and make breathing harder. A number of conditions can lead to it, such as infections, heart failure, cancer, and disorders of the kidneys or liver. Patients often experience shortness of breath, coughing, chest discomfort, and tiredness. To diagnose it, doctors generally perform a physical exam and order imaging, such as a chest X-ray or a computed tomography (CT) scan. Management may consist of draining the extra fluid with a procedure known as thoracentesis, treating the disease responsible for the fluid, or combining both approaches. Occasionally, surgical intervention is required to correct the underlying problem.

Using a personal credit card for business expenses is legal and very common, especially for sole proprietors, freelancers, and new businesses that haven't yet qualified for a business card. The expenses stay tax deductible as long as they are ordinary and necessary for your business. The IRS cares about what was purchased and why, not which card paid for it. Still, the approach carries risks and administrative burdens worth understanding.

The biggest concern is commingling personal and business finances. Mixing them on one statement makes bookkeeping harder, increases the chance of missing deductions or claiming personal items by mistake, and complicates an audit. If you go this route, keep receipts, note the business purpose of each charge, and record business transactions in your accounting software or a spreadsheet as they happen. Some people dedicate one personal card exclusively to business use, which keeps most of the convenience while greatly simplifying records.

If your business is an LLC or corporation, the stakes are higher. Regularly paying company expenses with personal funds, or the reverse, can weaken the legal separation between you and the business, which in a lawsuit could help a creditor argue for "piercing the corporate veil" and reaching your personal assets. The usual practice is to have the company reimburse you through an accountable plan: you submit documented expenses, the business pays you back, and the reimbursement is not taxable income to you while the business takes the deduction. Without such a plan, you might be treated as making a capital contribution or, in some corporate setups, lose the deduction at the business level.

Interest is another consideration. Interest on a personal card is generally not deductible, but the portion attributable to business purchases can be, if you can clearly trace and allocate it. That tracking is tedious when personal and business charges share a balance, which is another reason to keep them separate or pay the card in full each month.

There are credit effects as well. Business spending on a personal card counts toward your personal credit utilization, so large expenses can lower your personal credit score even if you pay on time. Personal cards also don't help your business build its own credit history. Many business cards still require a personal guarantee and a personal credit check, but most don't report routine activity to the personal bureaus, which keeps your personal utilization lower.

On the positive side, personal cards often carry stronger consumer protections under the federal CARD Act, such as limits on certain rate increases, which business cards don't receive. Rewards on personal cards can be competitive, though business cards often offer bonus categories aimed at office supplies, advertising, shipping, and travel, along with free employee cards and expense-tracking tools.

For a small sole proprietorship just starting out, a dedicated personal card used carefully is perfectly workable. As revenue grows, or if you've formed an LLC or corporation, moving to a separate business checking account and business credit card usually saves time, reduces legal and tax risk, and makes it easier to see how the business is actually performing. A tax professional can help you set up an accountable plan or sort out past mixed expenses if needed.

Worrying about your health is pretty normal, and looking after your body and your head both matter. That said, prostate cancer at 15 is extremely unlikely. It's a disease that mostly shows up in older men, so you can take a breath on that one. Anxiety pops up for everyone now and then, though, and if it's sticking around and messing with your day-to-day, it's worth talking to someone about it. A mental health professional can help you figure out where the worry is coming from and give you some practical ways to handle it. Honestly, there's no wrong time to start looking after your mental health, and reaching out for support when things feel heavy is a good call.

A market-on-close order is an instruction to trade a security at whatever price prevails when the trading session ends. Its purpose is to exit an existing position, whether that means selling a holding or buying back a short. Day traders often rely on it to make sure they finish the session flat, and long-term investors may use it to reduce their exposure by liquidating positions just before the close.

A typical raccoon litter usually contains between two and five babies, commonly called kits. Three or four is the most frequent number, and litters of six or more are uncommon. Females give birth once a year, typically in spring, and the kits stay with their mother for roughly a year before striking out on their own.

Chinese New Year is traditionally celebrated for 15 days. The festivities begin on the first day of the lunar calendar's first month, which falls between late January and mid-February, and end with the Lantern Festival on the fifteenth day, when people light lanterns, eat sweet rice dumplings called tangyuan, and often watch lion dances. Preparations, such as cleaning the house and shopping, usually start days or even weeks earlier, and the reunion dinner on New Year's Eve is one of the most important parts of the celebration.

The official public holiday is much shorter. In mainland China, the Spring Festival holiday is usually about seven or eight days, often arranged by shifting weekend working days. In places like Hong Kong, Taiwan, Singapore, and Malaysia, the public holiday typically lasts two to five days.

Yeah, it's definitely possible you're feeling pain after hernia repair. Hernias can come back after surgery, especially if whatever caused them in the first place hasn't been dealt with, or if the area keeps getting strained. Sometimes the pain is just scar tissue forming or a muscle spasm, which is annoying but not necessarily a sign something's wrong. Either way, bring it up with your surgeon or your primary care doctor. They can look at what's going on and figure out the actual cause. And stick to whatever post-op instructions you were given: skip the heavy lifting or straining, take your pain meds as prescribed, and don't skip those follow-up appointments.

A gravity boost lets a spacecraft use a planet's gravity to alter its speed and direction. Think of sitting on a playground swing while someone pushes you to send you higher. A planet can give a spacecraft a similar kind of push. When a spacecraft comes near a planet, the planet's gravity tugs on it and tries to draw it inward. If the craft is moving quickly enough, it won't crash into the planet but will instead settle into an orbit around it. However, if the spacecraft arrives at precisely the right speed and angle, it can use that gravity to "slingshot" around the planet, changing both its speed and its heading. This maneuver is known as a gravity assist, and people sometimes call it a gravity boost. Suppose a spacecraft is traveling toward Jupiter and needs more speed. It can pass close to the planet and let Jupiter's gravity propel it. As the craft draws nearer, gravity pulls it along and it accelerates. Then, as it curves around the far side of Jupiter, it leaves moving much faster than when it arrived. With gravity assists, spacecraft can reach distant regions of the solar system far more quickly and at lower cost than if they depended only on their own engines.

Dialysis tubes are thin tubes made from a semipermeable membrane, a material with microscopic pores that let small molecules and water pass through while blocking larger ones. They are usually made of cellulose or similar materials and are used in laboratories to separate molecules by size. A common use is to remove salts, small molecules, or unwanted solutes from a sample of protein or DNA: the sample is sealed inside the tube, which is then placed in a large volume of buffer or water, and the small contaminants gradually diffuse out through the pores while the larger target molecules stay inside. The tubing is sold in various pore sizes, measured by molecular weight cutoff, so users can choose one that retains the molecules they want to keep. Dialysis tubing is also used in teaching demonstrations of diffusion and osmosis, and it is the basic principle behind the artificial kidney machines used in medicine, which filter waste from a patient's blood in a similar way.

Oprah has given a lot of money to schools over the years, and she's especially known for the Oprah Winfrey Leadership Academy for Girls in South Africa. She opened it in 2007 as a boarding school for girls from poor backgrounds, and people have praised it for how it teaches students. She's also donated to plenty of other schools and education programs, both back home in the US and overseas, mostly aimed at kids who wouldn't otherwise get a fair shot.

I'm sorry you and your family are dealing with this. Repeated episodes of sudden hyper, aggressive behavior, followed by regret, over about ten years and now happening several times a day, need a proper psychiatric evaluation. This is treatable, and the fact that he feels remorse afterward is a useful sign that he can engage with help.

The right person to see is a psychiatrist, a medical doctor who specializes in mental health and can prescribe medication. If you are in India, which your wording suggests, you can go to a government hospital's psychiatry department, a district mental health program, or a larger teaching hospital such as a NIMHANS center or a medical college psychiatry unit. A private psychiatrist or a hospital's psychiatry department also works well. Ask for an appointment and be ready to describe the pattern: when the outbursts started, how often they happen, what seems to trigger them, whether they come on suddenly, whether he sleeps well, whether there are periods of unusually high energy or very low mood, whether he uses alcohol or other substances, and whether he has any head injuries or medical conditions. Keeping a short diary of episodes for a week or two can help the doctor a great deal.

Sudden, repeated aggression with high energy can be linked to several conditions, including bipolar disorder, intermittent explosive disorder, personality or impulse-control problems, substance effects, thyroid or other medical issues, and sometimes brain-related causes. Only an evaluation can sort this out, and the treatment depends on the cause. It often involves medication, such as mood stabilizers or other agents, along with counseling or behavioral therapy.

Until he is seen, your safety and that of others matters most. If he is about to hurt someone, move people away from him and, if needed, call emergency services (112 in India) or go to the nearest emergency department. Avoid confronting him during an episode, keep your voice calm and your distance, and do not try to restrain him yourself. Also consider getting support for yourself, since living with this is stressful.

On the Canadian T4 slip, Box 39, labelled "Employment income," shows the total employment income an employee earned over the tax year. That figure covers salary, wages, bonuses, and any other compensation paid by the employer. Box 38, labelled "Total insurable earnings," records the employee's insurable earnings for the year. It includes all of the employment income the employee earned, along with any extra amounts that are subject to Employment Insurance (EI) premiums.

Generally, if the employee received EI benefits during the tax year, the amount in box 39 should be reported as half of the amount in box 38. EI benefits are paid to people who cannot work for a time because of illness, injury, pregnancy, or the care of a newborn or adopted child. A person who receives EI benefits must pay EI premiums, which are figured as a percentage of insurable earnings. To work out how much an employee owes in premiums, the Canada Employment Insurance Commission (CEIC) relies on the figure in box 38 of the T4.

An employee who got EI benefits during the year should therefore enter half of their insurable earnings, as shown in box 38, in box 39. The reasoning is that premiums are only payable on half of those earnings.

Note also that the figure in box 39 may feed into the calculation of other taxes and credits, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP) contributions, Quebec Pension Plan (QPP) contributions, and the GST/HST credit. Reporting it accurately helps ensure your tax return reflects the correct taxes and credits.

Nuance Communications is an American technology company best known for its work in speech recognition and conversational artificial intelligence. Headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, it became one of the most influential firms in voice technology, developing software that allows computers to understand spoken language, transcribe dictation, and respond to people through natural conversation. In March 2022, Microsoft completed its acquisition of Nuance for roughly 19.7 billion dollars, and the company now operates as a subsidiary of Microsoft.

The company's history is somewhat complex because the modern Nuance resulted from a merger. A company called ScanSoft, which grew out of the document scanning and optical character recognition business originally associated with Xerox, acquired an earlier speech recognition firm named Nuance in 2005 and adopted its name. Over the following years, Nuance expanded aggressively through acquisitions, buying many smaller speech and language technology companies, which helped it build a dominant position in the field.

One of Nuance's most widely known products is Dragon, often called Dragon NaturallySpeaking in its earlier versions. Dragon is dictation software that lets users speak to their computers to type documents, send emails, and control applications. It became popular with professionals, people with disabilities, and anyone who preferred speaking to typing.

Healthcare became Nuance's most important market. Its Dragon Medical products help doctors and clinicians dictate patient notes directly into electronic health records, saving time on documentation. The company later developed more advanced tools, such as Dragon Ambient eXperience, often referred to as DAX, which listens to conversations between doctors and patients and automatically generates clinical notes. This focus on reducing the administrative burden on healthcare workers was a major reason Microsoft was interested in acquiring the company.

Nuance also built technology for businesses and consumer devices. It provided voice systems for customer service call centers, virtual assistants for banks and telecom companies, voice biometrics that verify a caller's identity by the sound of their voice, and speech technology for automobiles. Its speech recognition engine was widely reported to have been involved in the early development of Apple's Siri. In 2019, Nuance spun off its automotive division into a separate company called Cerence.

In short, Nuance Communications is a pioneer in teaching computers to understand human speech, with its greatest impact in healthcare documentation and enterprise customer engagement, and it now forms part of Microsoft's broader artificial intelligence and cloud efforts.

Your count of 42 million per mL is within the normal range. The concern is motility. About 20% of your sperm move forward well, which is below the usual reference value, and about half of your sperm show some movement, with 30% immotile. Your doctor is right to focus on this, and the pus cells, which doctors call leukocytes or leukocytospermia, are an important clue.

Yes, infection or inflammation can be a cause. White blood cells in semen produce reactive oxygen species, which damage sperm membranes and DNA and reduce motility. Infections of the prostate, epididymis, urethra, or seminal vesicles are common causes, and sexually transmitted infections such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, and mycoplasma should be specifically excluded. Because of this, the 10-day antibiotic course is the right first step. Take the full course exactly as prescribed, even if you feel better sooner, and do not stop or switch medicines on your own. Ask your doctor whether a semen culture and STI testing are needed, and whether your partner should be tested too if you have a sexual relationship.

Do not repeat the semen analysis immediately after the antibiotics. Sperm take roughly 2 to 3 months to fully regenerate, so a repeat test about 3 months after completing treatment will show whether the infection was the main cause. If the pus cells and low motility persist, your doctor may recommend a scrotal ultrasound to check for a varicocele, a common and treatable cause of poor motility, along with blood tests for hormones such as testosterone, FSH, LH, prolactin, and thyroid function.

Several general measures can also help. Stop smoking, cut back on alcohol, and avoid recreational drugs. Maintain a healthy weight and exercise regularly, but avoid prolonged heat exposure such as hot tubs, saunas, or laptops resting on the lap. Wear loose underwear, sleep well, and manage stress. A diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, fish, and nuts provides antioxidants and nutrients like zinc, folate, and omega-3 fatty acids, which support sperm health, though evidence that supplements alone fix motility is limited. Avoid taking supplements or hormones without medical supervision, since some can suppress sperm production.

If motility stays low after infection is treated and other causes are addressed, a fertility specialist (andrologist or reproductive urologist) can discuss options. Assisted methods such as intrauterine insemination or IVF with ICSI, where a single healthy sperm is injected into an egg, are highly effective even with reduced motility.

No, they are different measures used in different contexts, although both express a return or profitability as a percentage.

Capitalization rate, or cap rate, is used mainly in real estate investing. It is calculated by dividing a property's net operating income by its current market value or purchase price. If a building generates 100,000 dollars a year in net operating income after operating expenses (but before mortgage payments, income taxes, and depreciation) and is worth 1,500,000 dollars, the cap rate is about 6.7 percent. It tells an investor the annual yield the property would produce if bought with all cash, and it is commonly used to compare properties or gauge market pricing and risk.

Net profit margin is a business accounting measure. It is calculated by dividing net income by total revenue. Net income here is what remains after all expenses, including cost of goods sold, operating costs, interest, and taxes. If a company earns 1,000,000 dollars in revenue and keeps 80,000 dollars as net profit, its net profit margin is 8 percent. It shows how much of each dollar of sales turns into profit, so it measures operating efficiency and pricing power.

The key differences are in the denominator and the question each answers. Cap rate compares income to the value of an asset, asking what return the asset yields relative to its price. Net profit margin compares profit to sales, asking how profitable the business's revenue is. Cap rate also uses income before financing costs and taxes, while net profit margin is after them.

The two can overlap in practice. A real estate company might report a net profit margin on its financial statements, while the properties it owns would each be evaluated with cap rates. But they should not be used interchangeably, and a figure for one cannot be substituted for the other.

Magnets cannot power a motor that runs indefinitely, since doing so would break the law of conservation of energy. That law holds that energy can neither be generated nor eliminated; it can only shift from one form into another. A motor needs an energy supply to operate, whether that comes from burning fuel, as in a car engine, or from electricity, as in a fan. Attempting to build a perpetual motion machine with magnets would mean keeping the motor going with no energy input at all, and that is impossible because energy cannot appear from nothing. Consider a toy car powered by a battery: the battery supplies the energy that moves the car, and once it is drained, the car stops. Unless the battery is replaced or another energy source is found, the car cannot keep moving. A perpetual motion machine is no different and cannot keep running without a steady supply of energy. Videos showing magnets making things move can be entertaining, but these devices cannot operate forever without some form of energy input.

Sir John Templeton, the legendary contrarian investor and founder of the Templeton funds, was warning against a recurring psychological trap: the belief that the normal rules of markets, valuation, and human behavior have somehow been suspended by new circumstances. When people say "this time it's different," they are usually justifying prices or behavior that would have looked reckless by historical standards, arguing that some novel development makes the old lessons irrelevant.

The core of his point is that markets move in cycles driven largely by human emotion, particularly greed and fear, and those emotions don't change much from one generation to the next. During a speculative boom, investors reach for explanations of why soaring prices are justified and sustainable. In the late 1920s, people believed a new era of permanent prosperity had arrived. In the late 1990s, many argued that the internet had rendered traditional measures like earnings and cash flow obsolete, so companies with no profits could be worth billions. Before 2008, a common belief was that nationwide housing prices couldn't fall because of new financial engineering and changes in lending. Each time, the story sounded compelling and contained some truth, since the internet really was transformative, but the conclusion that valuation no longer mattered proved disastrous.

Templeton was not saying that nothing ever changes. Technologies, industries, and economic structures genuinely do evolve, and he acknowledged that. His warning was aimed at using change as a rationalization for abandoning discipline. The danger lies in the specific moment when investors stop asking whether they are paying a sensible price for an asset because they have convinced themselves that a new paradigm makes such questions outdated. That reasoning tends to appear near the peaks of bubbles, precisely when risk is highest.

This fits his broader contrarian philosophy, captured in another of his famous lines, that bull markets are born on pessimism, grow on skepticism, mature on optimism, and die on euphoria. "This time it's different" is the language of euphoria. Templeton built his fortune by doing the opposite of the crowd, buying when others were despairing and being cautious when others were exuberant. His advice amounts to a reminder to respect history, stay humble about one's ability to predict a new era, and anchor decisions in fundamentals like earnings, value, and price rather than in the excitement of a compelling narrative.

A monarch is basically the person at the top of a monarchy, which is a system where one individual, usually a king or queen, has supreme authority over a country. Monarchs usually get the job by inheritance, so the crown gets passed down through a royal family. They're the head of state, which means they represent the country abroad and handle a lot of the ceremonial stuff. Depending on the country, a monarch might also hold some executive or legislative power, but that varies a lot from one system to another. Most of the time they lean on a council of ministers or other officials for advice, and many live under constitutional limits that keep their power in check.

Investing young is a smart move, and it can really pay off over time if you stick with it. Before you dive in, though, get your house in order. Build an emergency fund so an unexpected bill doesn't force you to sell investments at a bad time, and pay off any high-interest debt first, since that's usually a guaranteed return you can't beat in the market. Set some clear goals too, whether that's retirement, a house, or something else.

Then do some homework. Investing can feel intimidating when you're just getting started, but the basics aren't that complicated. Read a few books or articles, maybe take a free online course, or sit down with a financial advisor who can explain how different options work and what risks come with them.

You don't need a big pile of cash to begin. Start small and add a bit each month. This is basically dollar-cost averaging, and it helps smooth out the ups and downs of the market so you're not betting everything on one day's prices.

Also, don't put all your eggs in one basket. Spread your money across different asset types like stocks, bonds, and some cash. If one category tanks, the others can help cushion the hit.

Mostly, be patient and think long term. Check in on your strategy every so often and tweak it when your situation or goals change. And if you're about to make a big move, it's worth talking to a professional who can build a plan around your specific circumstances.

Teeth may yellow for several different reasons. A frequent culprit is the buildup of plaque and tartar on tooth surfaces. Plaque is a sticky bacterial film that clings to teeth; when brushing and flossing fail to remove it, it can harden into tartar, which is hard to get rid of and can give teeth a yellowish cast. Other causes of yellowing include drinking staining beverages such as coffee, tea, and red wine, using tobacco products that discolor teeth, aging, which thins the enamel and makes the dentin beneath it more noticeable, and taking certain medications that can alter tooth color. Brushing for an hour will not make your teeth dramatically whiter. Brushing and flossing do help remove plaque and keep tartar from building up, but they cannot replace professional whitening. Professional whitening uses specialized products and procedures to lift stains and discoloration, leaving teeth brighter. It can be performed in a dental office or done at home with a whitening kit. If you want whiter teeth, speaking with a dentist is the best way to figure out the most suitable approach for you.

It is not always feasible for a plane in trouble to make an emergency landing on water, since its position and the state of the water can make such an attempt difficult or even impossible. If a plane is flying too high or is too far from the surface, for instance, it may lack the time or distance needed to glide down safely. The water could also be too choppy for a secure touchdown, or ships or buildings might be in the way. Still, there are times when planes do come down on water and people survive. The 2009 Hudson River landing, in which Captain Chesley "Sully" Sullenberger set a plane down on the river in New York City, is a well-known case. There, the aircraft was flying at a low altitude and no obstacles stood in its path, which allowed the landing to happen. Passengers and crew were also able to leave the aircraft quickly and reach safety. In many other incidents, however, no one survives a crash onto water. This may happen because the impact is too violent, because the plane sinks before everyone can escape, or because the water is too cold or turbulent to survive. It is also worth noting that many plane crashes occur on land rather than water, and survival odds depend heavily on the particular circumstances of each crash.

Pain in the chest and between the shoulder blades may stem from many different conditions, and a precise diagnosis isn't possible without further details and a medical examination. Discomfort on the right side of the chest might result from issues such as a strained muscle, a fractured or bruised rib, or something far more serious, like a heart attack. Pain in the shoulder blade area can likewise arise from several sources, including a strained or injured muscle, a compressed nerve, or a spinal problem. If you have chest and shoulder blade pain along with cold or flu-like symptoms, you should contact a healthcare provider promptly. Your symptoms may well be linked to the flu, yet other possible causes should also be ruled out. A healthcare provider can assess your condition, perform a physical exam, and perhaps order tests to identify the source of your pain and recommend the most suitable treatment. If you experience severe chest pain or trouble breathing, seek emergency medical care right away, since these signs may point to a serious illness that needs immediate attention.

Real estate investment trusts, or REITs, can be an effective way to earn passive income. They let investors purchase shares in a collection of properties that produce revenue, including commercial buildings and apartment complexes. Most REITs distribute part of their earnings to shareholders as dividends, which creates a steady flow of income. Still, as with any investment, REITs involve risk and may not fit everyone's needs. Before deciding to invest, you should think carefully about your goals, how much risk you can tolerate, and your overall financial circumstances. Spreading your money across several kinds of assets is also wise, instead of depending too heavily on a single type of investment. To judge whether REITs make sense for you, look closely at the particular ones you're considering, evaluating their financial results, the quality of their management, and any other factors that could affect their risk and potential returns. Speaking with a financial advisor or other professional before you make any investment decisions is also advisable.

Random optimization is basically finding a good solution by guessing at random and keeping the best guess.
